(C.I.S.) Office Notes
File No. 80. Dx
February 25, 1929.

Departure of Harbin Detectives
with prisoner for Harbin.

Mr. Van Chen Bun, Det. Baranoff, Det. Bauss
and the Chinese detective and prisoner Ushakov left
Shanghai for Harbin via Dairen in the s.s. "Sakaki
Maru" at 2 p.m. February 23. It is the intention of
the D.C.I. of the Harbin Police to break his journey
at Tsingtao to take Belgoanoff into custody and
continue his journey on the same ship to Dairen.

V. ...y

哈爾濱偵探押送囚犯前往哈爾濱。

范陳本先生（Van Chen Bun）、巴拉諾夫偵探（Det. Baranoff）、鮑斯偵探（Det. Bauss）以及一名華籍偵探和囚犯烏沙科夫（Ushakov）於2月23日下午2時乘「榊丸」號（Sakaki Maru）輪船經大連離開上海前往哈爾濱。哈爾濱警察局副總監意圖在青島中途停留，將別洛加諾夫（Belgoanoff）逮捕，並繼續乘坐同一艘輪船前往大連。

V. ...y

(C.I.D.) Office Notes
February 16, 1929
A/B.C.1.
With reference to the attached file I beg to
report that on February 16, 1929 the accused A. Unlakoff was
again brought before the Provisional Court when the case
was concluded and he was ordered handed over to Det.
baranoff representative of the Harbin Police.
In connection with the above case the following telegram
was received on February 15:
" Municipal Police Shanghai
Melgunoff arrested send police escort, Tsingtao Police
Headquarters.
Artoshkowitz "
Melgunoff's arrest was effected through the
assistance of I.C.S. agents who for six months have been
trailing and watching Melgunoff in town.
I. Orlanikof
D.S.
Foreign Section,
What arrangements are being
made regarding Melghunoff's transfer
to Harbin?
16/2/29

關於附件檔案，謹報告如下：1929年2月16日，被告 A. Unlakoff 再次被提審至臨時法院，案件審結，並下令將其移交給代表哈爾濱警方的巴拉諾夫偵探（Det. baranoff）。
關於上述案件，於2月15日收到以下電報：
「上海工部局警察
梅爾古諾夫（Melgunoff）已逮捕，請派警護送，青島警察總局。
阿托什科維茨（Artoshkowitz）」
梅爾古諾夫的逮捕是通過工部局警務處特工的協助實現的，這些特工已在市內跟蹤和監視梅爾古諾夫六個月。

Translation of a letter addressed to the
Director of Criminal Investigation Department in
Shanghai, dated Harbin, 8th day of the 18th year of
the Chinese Republic, No. 30.

I have sent J.I. Detective Inspectors BJUKOFF,
Vasilii Nikolaevich and Peng Ming Yuen to search for and to
apprehend Turgens, Vladimir Nikolaevich, who is charged
with having received money from the American City Bank in
Harbin by means of fraudulent cheques.

I shall be much obliged if you will kindly
render them assistance in handing over the arrested man
named BJUKOFF to be conducted to Harbin.

sd.    Chief of Detective Department
sd.    Chief Clerk of the Department.

布福大供詞（譯文）

吾名布福大年廿二歲以前並未犯罪已有妻室俄國僑民生長於莫斯科現住康
那夜街二十五号于一月廿五日謹供如左
吾于一九二〇年自俄國知難民到哈爾濱家有一母一姊二弟他們現住拉石地而那夜
街双号門牌吾自幼受充分教育在一九二六年中季吾在馬斯脫未約街花旗銀行
得一間者之職嗣該銀行給吾以儲蓄部會計之職在一九二八年八月廿五日停職緣吾
每當遲到早歸之故在該行任職時吾得一妻然因此受經濟壓迫停職後在中華民
國十七年十月内吾請吾前行中同事「居考夫」借日金一百元據伊說伊同他數人
用自簽支票法已騙得款項数次「居考夫」允許第二日給吾日金一百元而且有
事與我商議翌日伊至我家約吾同出伊給吾一簽字証該証主人在行内存有大
宗款項再並允給我一空自支票命吾照簽再尋一人至行内持支票支款吾遂
應允並尋一相當之人此事廢時多日一日吾訪一友名「來廣」住「阿匹脫卡司卡夜街
卅六号在彼家中遇一人名「佛蘭士」吾同「佛蘭士」同出伊告我現在無業甚困苦吾即

將支票員簽事與商並請伊符票去領款伊諾之吾遂立至居考夫處告之當日
居考夫給我一簽字証上有名字曰「北板西」吾練習簽字三天逐向居考夫取一空
白支票他任看太斯加斯加街給吾翌日吾在居考夫家遂將北板西之名簽于支
票在此街時遇佛蘭士二人遂乘汽車至銀行既里他入內吾守于車內待他取
得錢出即同至鐵路办事处打電話給居考夫問此事如何得回音曰甚滿意吾等
遂再回銀行吾仍坐於車中佛蘭士則持以年十二月三号之換款証数五千一百元
金洋至行支款行中照當日日金市价如数給之吾分得日金二千二百元居考夫得日
金五千元餘給佛蘭士居考夫之款在當晚吾皇伊家與之吾所得之洋已用去
對於假支票A字帽冒名「納夫推令」其数二千一百元金洋佛蘭士至行領款未得之
事吾完全不知佛蘭士之人吾見之必可証實捕沙考夫吾未見過亦不認識以上二
人現在何處亦不知吾閱此案再無他言可述

壹千九百念九年正月廿四号（哈尔滨）
關於紐約銀行被人陸續用賈支票領去日洋兩萬七千壹百五十二元三角三分余等
（警務處刑事稽查科探長）詢問在押犯人得下列供單
朱尔考夫阿立克山大阿立克人独老惟去年廿七岁屋宿通克司人未犯过罪有妻俄國
（11）僑民墨使哥生最住在色去到惟西街一百另八号云供單如下
余在紐約銀行充現存及儲蓄部商業主任由壹千九百廿八年四号二号始在夏季某月
余在開泰司閘亞街遇見余老友惟賴狄末凡考拉惟去歐情司我兩人乃同行至森加利
海灘該时余友即对我云用賈支票向銀行取係狠便当的事当彼语我时使
我回憶前我在某銀行執事时所有空白支票並無人管理且無論何人祇要
說出某存款人姓名即能領得預存支票我乃將此事告知余友歐情司彼云此

事甚佳並云彼當研究支票上之簽名式我即允許歐性司任調查存款人姓名及
所存之數歐性司乃囑余調查亞昆及路白那惟去兩人之存款數目若干余等之談
話終止於此乃分手別去在第二次會面時我乃將亞昆及路白那惟去二人款數告知
歐性司亞昆之存款數係日洋四千元而路白那惟去之存款係美金一萬一千元後乃
議決用賈支票在亞昆存款內支取洋三百元此後歐性司常至銀行研究銀行人
員檢驗支票之手續在去年十月初歐性司由某銀行執事馬而子者處得著
(2)
預存支票一張（該銀行執員與本案並無關係）於同日余在抽屜內覓得卡片一張
上有亞昆簽名我即將該卡片交与歐性司在雪羅卡亞街上翌日晨歐性
司將原卡片還我並示我賈支票一張計日洋三百元元亞昆簽名歐性
司並對我云彼在哈爾濱頗名相識者故不能親赴銀行取款但彼決將此
事另託一人名由雪考夫此人當日我亦遇見隔日早有一人持該賈支票至
我所僱用之銀行我將該票收下並出收據与來人來人乃持票去因付款伕待
該行支票經過數次檢查後交与付銀處放能領款約十五分鐘或廿分鐘後

歐性司由電話內詢問余經過之手續余乃告彼手續皆完備由雪考夫乃回至
余行將款領去至午後兩點時我乃至英司吐惟亞街上之矮開秋店內遇見歐性
司彼乃授我支票一張號碼196035計洋一百元為我之應得份子後繼續由雪考
夫持票支票至我之銀行兌現共得日洋二仟七百元支票號碼係1880我個人分
得日洋一仟元該款由歐性司在原路上授我此後余表示不願繼續該行不正當行
為但歐性司嚇我云彼当寫匿名信至我所受僱之銀控告我之作弊行為而彼則
離哈爾濱他去我乃被迫繼續該項不正當之手續我此後又授給歐性司支票兩張
計洋三千兩百及三千一百其號碼為03295及03294存戶名路山那維去以上兩支
票由雪考夫來行兌現我由歐性司處分得日洋四千七百元並由歐性司还我日
洋三百元該款係前付入西昆名下之錢因風欲使人不疑之故末次領款後歐
性司云彼須赴申並告我由雪考夫亦已離哈南去約十二月間我接得歐性司
由上海寄我一信詢問我之情形我即回信至上海亞飛路六百三十六号此後
我並未遇見歐性司至於由雪考夫究竟何往並其姓名之真偽則不得而知但

我能認得其面目若遇見之我曾遇見一人名葛力葛雷物賴狄米羅惟去矮服夫此
人前亦在紐約銀行內辦事葛向我借洋一百元我允隔日交彼当时我乃告彼
使用買支票之事並叫伊加入此舉起而葛不允徒乃加入並云彼自巳能簽他
人之名但只另覓他人任兌欵一二日後葛打電話与我約我在別直惟亞克
通司克耶路候彼我乃至所約地点遇彼彼乃告我彼已覓得一人加入所謀之事
並要我与此人見面但我拒絕彼之請求同日晚上葛至我家告我云彼所覓得
之人名法淪志隔日我携一名片至葛處該名片係銀行存戶之一葛乃仿名片之
簽字練習之隔日葛在我房間內簽該存戶之名於支票上当时乃决定遣人持票
至銀行領欵其手續与前数次同樣此次所領之數為日洋一萬另八百卅
六元六角五分当日夜間葛携日洋五千元付我作為我應得之數葛並告我
此後彼不願再從事此项工作但法賴志迫其繼續從事法賴志彼云如彼不
允其請求將彼不法之事宣佈我亦不願再繼續此项不法行為此後法賴志
乃单独從事由銀行內取得預存支票冒簽南夫得林名該票號碼為32387

彼親自携交銀行付銀處執員斷定此票係冒簽者故不允付錢而持
該張支票者即告失蹤此事發生於去年十一月底銀行執事疑我與此
案有關我即承認我所犯不法之事並供葛係我之同謀者我能指認法
賴志如遇見之關於賈支票領款一役我共分得洋一萬另八百元我共
用日洋六千一百十八元買銀槍器及他種銀器代我岳父還債計日洋兩千
元付雕刻匠日洋六十元作為借款英洋二百七十五元付与醫生付徐考夫六十元
付米狄林英洋六百元又寄日洋三百元至俄國其餘一千三百八十七元回洋
係我個人用去所有銀器值洋一千三百八十七在徐考夫及醫生發物史敢處
後由彼等將該項銀器交与銀行執事此外銀行並得我付亞昆云日洋
三百元我應得之薪水日洋一百元養老金日洋五十元我之存款日洋九
百五十元並我之金錶一只值日洋一百五十元該錶我於一千九百廿七年所買
此是我之口供無誤

住右緬長司克佛耶街素而貌拉獨飯房二多房間
收年元月七号供
我於昨年二月，米而老天際立克山大阪主之人我老姐之首光朱清診治而認識。我診治他計有八月之久而尚欠少數津貼之元。
且此半年月底米而考夫之病已治愈並要求我遠赴清徽區費。係因他擬結婚而需款托殷。至上月內米而考夫又來請
求診斷他身體之健全。斯時我中代他索欠他同訪該日寄送米民旗銀行支票一紙以清前欠當日即有米女老夫送木
條克夫簽名支票一紙。次日即向銀行支取。我不認識徐氏夫（何人得五日之前日調小記）有某手輕少年送米米而老夫
之名片一串收價北箱子二只並要求代為保藏。該院米而老夫親自前來據訪該箱由廊館意並請保藏。係因他已遷居
冷靜地段與菜拜等廠附近而搬遷故。我即信米而老夫所言而代為保藏。該院有不知姓名二人持有米而老夫名片
附己前來我家。要求將銀器拿出。我即交給他八感十米而考夫之不法而隱藏行的新元生不和。米而考夫之借單
說他借那片號五元本不付的

票復司風簽字

譯文
米而考夫阿立克山大隊立克人從老惟公之附供
以手三日扶新志得流交。而被業復日風医士診治有八月之久。至去年十一月（日期不记）我觉身能不起。又使業後习风这士诊流
斯叶伯叩個找退而前次。我问他又数。他说共一症之一後吃。我印送他但的银行支票一票。计程丈由徐走夫签名。去年
十月初我以石传托徐支夫所检符耶松来谁去出他自己陆吾代有口洋二千之之之但的银行。徐克夫即问我何来此種鉅
款而何故要他出名代存。我回称该款由此事没营而未种之所以不用自己姓名存储者。有恐银行要疑我何来此种
鉅款。徐克夫信我之言。而代已存储。我後陸續将款提出。心薄上存有日洋徐克夫出面代存此款并无酬劳。
惟第一次同安险资大在一件白我情南京借洋六千元。数日前我托徐克夫持我在片送有一百二六内储作器。出业後习周
保存。该院押人親自必买医士處积求保有该祠在不用。言以新分三城市隔離颐与聚拜写离相近。懼盗纽改耳。
當蒙贵医士面许准行。该院我爱银行经理、我计被他拘范）、嘱咐。伤人持我在片往获医士處摄取相小。而转放在银行内
在我第一保单内我说我不给荣医士洋次值，费。乃我不敢便官长信那叠泾志三疯。京耕此事因我个人而与被拘当
事项些境桥事赏言。我对世法医士及生元老的他的诊费也。
此供已经宣读過

徐克夫，即格行，即格來維云，供單
中國籍人 信基督教理人
年花甲 未犯罪過
住居馬地那哥，柏司格耶街十六號

我服務在毫國鈔店，由哪年在軍官學校即認識米而老夫，阿立克山大，阿立克山人貌女佳士。我們以米而考夫為好人，並不意科及他
能于非法事牽涉。我完全信托他。大約在去年十月間米而考夫托我代購銀質寶盒一只計洋二千元。該款由他自办。我因不能記
憶該房招所，推問設在何處司得耶從斯時米而考夫托我代購。希圖價格略廉。緣司他与議價而未得廉價購之。去年十月初米而考夫，
交我洋一千五百元用籌措各存儲銀行。為因他身為銀行職員。若以他自己姓名存儲許多款項。銀行必起疑竇。而与我位
有関。我即問他何来着多銀錢。米而老夫答称。彼經營数件生意頗为順手。我即意想米而老夫之丈人经商頗富。他不願
以資本顯露于親戚间以免告貸也。我即允诺。而以日洋五千多元用我姓名存儲於紐約银行。此款是米而老夫的。後他陸
續向銀行提取。而祇有日洋拾元。出哪年元月生了晚米而考夫到我家来。请我将在我家内之銀宝盒送出。素復可同医士處，
他言我之銀行有何等司而後去。我想问他有何事發生。而他于倉忙间未答而去。該箱按上項借收。在去年十月间由我代購而貯以
在我處者。即米而考夫要亦存放我處。因他家離市較遠，而懼盗劫也。去年十二月初米而老夫嘱我往耶媽司克耶街一薩埵博夫，
銀匠處代取器。該銀件在銀匠處刻完。我即代往而取得銀件。米而老夫竟欲将一切物件經在一處。而要置我處。哪年元月
廿五号我将物件送至素復司同医士處。我於音與该事完全無份。並無丝毫通同。我因太信仰米而老夫而受他利用。此素該
銀行經理乃受損失最大。而銀行已良决是國飯店关于我自对于此案完全恢復舊狀。我並未向米而老夫索取酬勞。惟他于一次借款
得六千元以賺大元一件。此情已对我宣過。而並无私謀。

紐約城市國家銀行總監柯蒂斯先生（Mr. Curtis）發現了六張支票，其中5張支票號碼為 03294、
03295、06267、17675、19080，金額合計為日元 27,152.33，
已被罪犯兌現。同時，一張偽造支票被提示付款，其號碼為 32257，
金額為日元 2,100，但未被銀行支付。
A. A. CHULKOFF，銀行職員，和 G.V. LVOFF，
一名被解僱的職員，承認犯了此罪。
現申請查找其餘罪犯並追回款項。

V. KUPLIANIKOFF，
銀行保管員。

OFFICIAL REPORT.

18th year of the Chinese Republic, January 29, Harbin.

We, Inspectors of the Detective Department of the Police
Administration of Special District of Eastern Provinces, named
SOSIK, FEDOROFF and BARANOFF made the official report to the
following effect:- At 8 p.m. to-day a report was received
by telephone from the New York City Bank on Mostovaya Street
that a discovery was made there of a large sum of money having
been received by means of forged cheques, the Bank having
detained two persons in connection with the case, whom the
Police are requested to take over for further investigation.
On arrival at the Bank we found detained there Alexander
Chulkoff, employee of the Bank and Grigory Lvoff, ex employee
of the same Bank. The men were taken to the Administration
before the Chief.

Inspectors SOSIK, FEDOROFF and BARANOFF

Identical with the original: Jd.
Chief Clerk of the Detective Department,

官 方 報 告。

中華民國十八年，1月29日，哈爾濱。

我們，東省特別區警察管理處偵查科的督察，
名為 SOSIK、FEDOROFF 和 BARANOFF，作出如下官方報告：- 今晚8點，
接到莫斯托瓦亞街（Mostovaya Street）紐約城市銀行的電話報告，稱
發現有一筆鉅款是通過偽造支票收取的，銀行已扣留了兩名
與此案有關的人員，請求警方接管以進行進一步調查。
到達銀行後，我們發現銀行職員亞歷山大·丘爾科夫（Alexander Chulkoff）
和同一家銀行的前職員格里戈里·利沃夫（Grigory Lvoff）被扣留在那裡。
這些人被帶到管理局局長面前。

督察 SOSIK、FEDOROFF 和 BARANOFF

Translation.
------------

OFFICIAL REPORT.

18th year of the Chinese Republic, January 24, Harbin.
We, Inspectors of the Detective Department of Police
Administration, FEDOROFF and SOSIK, made this official report
to the following effect: In accordance with the report made
by Vladimir Nikolaevich, KUPLENNIKOFF, Custodian of the New
York City National Bank that the sum of Yen 27,152.33 was
received from the Bank at different times by means of forged
cheques, by order of the Chief of Department questioned and
obtained the statements given from the persons detained in
connection with the case:-

Statement of CHULKOFF, Alexander Alexandrovich,
27 years of age, Orthodox, no previous
conviction, married, Russian emigrant, native of
Moscow, residing at No. 108 Pochtovaya Street.

"I am an employee of the International City Bank on
Mostovaya Street, in charge of commercial powers of attorney
of the Current and Savings Accounts. Have been in this
employ since April 2 last of the 17th year of Chinese Republic.
Sometime in the Summer, I do not remember in which month, I
met on the Kitaiskaya Street an old acquaintance of mine
Vladimir Nikolaevich URGENS. In the course of the general
conversation the latter was interested to know where I was
employed and requested my assistance in obtaining a loan
of about ten thousand Yen from somewhere or other. Having
told URGENS that I was not in a position to help him in this
matter, the conversation ended there and we parted. URGENS
told me that he was living in Shanghai and was trading in furs.
A few days later I again met URGENS on the Kitaiskaya Street
and we walked to the Sungari foreshore. This time he expressed
a thought that it would be easy to obtain money from a bank
by means of forged documents. I then remembered that in the
Bank, where I was employed, there was absolutely no control
over blank cheques i.e. any person mentioning the name of
the person who has a current account easily obtained a
reserve cheque, and I told URGENS this. The latter said this
was good and that he himself would see to the signature on
the cheques. I gave URGENS my consent to assist him in
carrying out the plan in question, i.e. I was to check whether
there were accounts and to what amount belonging to certain
people as for instance OKUN and RUBANOVICH, whom URGENS
pointed out to me himself. The conversation ended there and
we parted. At the next meeting I gave URGENS the Balances
of accounts of OKUN and RUBANOVICH, the former's being 4000 Yen
and the latter's 11,000 Gold Dollars, U.S.A. currency. It was
decided to try and present first a cheque for a small sum up
to 300 Yen from OKUN's account. URGENS became a frequent
visitor to the Bank to study the method of the passing of
cheques. At the beginning of October, last year, I do not
remember the date, URGENS obtained in the Bank from an
employee named MALTZ, who has nothing to do with the case in
question, one reserve cheque. On that same day I got out
from a drawer a card signed by OKUN and handed it over at
the closing time of the Bank to URGENS, who was waiting for
me on the Shirokaya Street. The following day in the
morning URGENS returned me the card and showed a filled in
and well signed cheque to the amount of 300 Yen with the name
of OKUN. URGENS stated that he was known to a great many
people in Harbin and he would not therefore present the
cheque for payment at the Bank himself, but would entrust it
page_data.zh:
譯文。
------------

官 方 報 告。

中華民國十八年，1月24日，哈爾濱。
我們，警察管理處偵查科的督察，FEDOROFF 和 SOSIK，作出如下官方報告：根據紐約城市國家銀行保管員弗拉基米爾·尼古拉耶維奇·庫普列尼科夫（Vladimir Nikolaevich, KUPLENNIKOFF）的報告，稱有人通過偽造支票在不同時間從銀行收取了日元 27,152.33，按照處長的命令，我們審問了與此案有關的被拘留人員並獲取了供詞：-

丘爾科夫（CHULKOFF），亞歷山大·亞歷山德羅維奇（Alexander Alexandrovich）的供詞，
27歲，東正教徒，無前科，已婚，俄羅斯移民，莫斯科人，居住在郵政街（Pochtovaya Street）108號。

「我是莫斯托瓦亞街國際城市銀行的職員，負責往來賬戶和儲蓄賬戶的商業授權委託書。自中華民國十七年4月2日起受僱於此。
去年夏天某個時候，我不記得是哪個月，我在基泰斯卡亞街（Kitaiskaya Street）遇到了我的老熟人弗拉基米爾·尼古拉耶維奇·烏爾根斯（Vladimir Nikolaevich URGENS）。在一般交談中，他對我在哪裡工作感興趣，並請求我幫助從某處獲得約一萬日元的貸款。告訴烏爾根斯我無法在此事上幫助他後，談話就此結束，我們分開了。烏爾根斯告訴我他住在上海，從事皮草貿易。
幾天後，我再次在基泰斯卡亞街遇到烏爾根斯，我們一起走到松花江岸邊。這次他表達了一個想法，認為通過偽造文件從銀行獲取資金很容易。我隨即想起在我工作的銀行裡，對空白支票根本沒有管控，即任何提到擁有往來賬戶的人名字的人都能輕易獲得備用支票，我把這一點告訴了烏爾根斯。後者說這很好，他自己會負責支票上的簽名。我同意烏爾根斯協助執行該計劃，即我要檢查某些人（例如烏爾根斯親自指給我的 OKUN 和 RUBANOVICH）是否有賬戶以及金額是多少。談話就此結束，我們分開了。在下一次見面時，我給了烏爾根斯 OKUN 和 RUBANOVICH 的賬戶餘額，前者為 4,000 日元，後者為 11,000 金美元（美國貨幣）。決定嘗試首先從 OKUN 的賬戶中提示一張小額支票，金額不超過 300 日元。烏爾根斯成為銀行的常客，以研究支票兌付的方法。去年10月初，我不記得到底是哪一天，烏爾根斯從一名與本案無關的名為 MALTZ 的職員那裡從銀行獲得了一張備用支票。就在當天，我從抽屜裡拿出一張由 OKUN 簽名的卡片，並在銀行關閉時交給了在希羅卡亞街（Shirokaya Street）等我的烏爾根斯。第二天早上，烏爾根斯還給我卡片，並展示了一張填寫完好、簽名良好的支票，金額為 300 日元，戶名為 OKUN。烏爾根斯聲稱他在哈爾濱認識很多人，因此他不會親自去銀行提示支票付款，而是將其委託

page_data.en:
- 2 -

to a man he knew, someone by the name of USHAKOFF, whose
first and second names he did not mention, and who appeared
that very day. On seeing the cheque I accepted it from the
bearer, put a number on it and issued him a receiving check,
upon which he went out of the Bank, as the actual receiving
of the money was to be effected by arrangement only when I
would inform them that the cheque had successfully passed
through the control and was handed in to the Cashier for
payment. About 15 or 20 minutes URGENS inquired by telephone
and I said that everything was in order. USHAKOFF then came
back to the Bank and got the money. About 2 p.m. I left the
Bank and proceeded to the Boulevard opposite the City Market
and Shop Arcade in Mostovaya Street, where URGENS was waiting
for me and I then received from him my share of the money
Yen 100 (Cheque No. 17675). In the same way and again through
USHAKOFF two thousand seven hundred (2700 Yen) were received
by cheque No. 19080 dated 13/X, from which amount I received
a thousand (1.000 Yen) from URGENS on the same Boulevard. After
that I refused to continue these transactions, but URGENS
threatened to send an anonymous letter to the Bank about me
whilst he would escape from Harbin. I was afraid of that and
was compelled to consent to continue issuing cheques. The next
two cheques Nos. 03295 and 03294 dated October 24 and 25 res-
pectively I handed myself to URGENS on the street as he was
not going to come to the Bank anymore and on these cheques
URGENS forged the signature of the owner of RUBANOVICH account
to the amounts of three thousand two hundred and three thousand
one hundred Yen. The money of the above cheques was also
received by USHAKOFF and I got from Urgens cash of four
thousand seven hundred (4700 Yen) and in addition to that 300
Yen, which Ushakoff owed me, for camouflaging purposes were
returned to the account of OKUN. After this last obtaining
of the money URGENS stated that he would temporarily discontinue
transactions with the cheques and was going to Shanghai, adding
that USHAKOFF had already left for the South. In December I
received a letter from Urgens in Shanghai in which he asked
if everything was alright. I answered him to Shanghai to the
address of 636 Avenue Joffre, Apt. 6. I did not see URGENS
anymore. Whether Ushakoff left Harbin and whether this was
his real name I do not know. I can identify him, however.
Sometime later I met Grigory Vladimirovich LVOFF, an ex
employee of the Bank, who asked me to lend him 100 Yen, which
I promised to give him the following day; at the same time
I related to him in detail the transactions with cheques
carried out through me and offered him to join me in continuing
the forging of the cheques. LVOFF at first hesitated to
consent, but eventually gave in and said that he would forge
the signatures on the cheques himself, but will find a man
to receive the money. In a day or two, I do not remember
exactly, LVOFF telephoned to me and arranged to meet corner
of Birjevaya and Kitaiskaya Streets, when he told me that he
found a man with whom he was about to make arrangements and
invited me to join him, but I refused. In the evening of the
same day LVOFF called at my house and said that the man found
was named FRANTZ and he consented to receive money by means
of forged cheques. The next day I brought to LVOFF's house
a card signed by the owner of an Account under the name of
POPEL and LVOFF after a little practice signed the cheque
on the following day in my room. It was then and there
decided to send the man to get this money from the Bank and
this was done in the same way as on previous occasions
by cheque No. 06267 dated November 3 to the amount of 5100
Gold Dollars, U.S.A. Currency. The money was paid out in
Yen at the rate of the day's exchange and amounted to Yen
10836.65. The same evening LVOFF brought to my house my
share five thousand (Yen 5000). LVOFF then told me that he
did not want to make any more forgeries, but the man named
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

交给他认识的一个名叫 USHAKOFF 的人，此人名字和姓氏他未提及，且于当日出现。见到支票后，我从持票人手中收下，编上号码并出具了一张收款回执，随后他便离开了银行，因为实际取款需待我通知他们支票已顺利通过审核并移交出纳付款时，方可按约定进行。约15或20分钟后，URGENS 打电话询问，我说一切正常。USHAKOFF 随后回到银行取走了钱款。下午2点左右，我离开银行，前往莫斯托瓦亚街（Mostovaya Street）城市市场和购物拱廊对面的林荫大道，URGENS 在那里等我，我从他那里收到了我的分成，即100日元（支票号17675）。以同样的方式，再次通过 USHAKOFF，凭10月13日开具的第19080号支票兑现了2700日元，从中我在同一条林荫大道从 URGENS 处收到了1000日元。此后我拒绝继续这些交易，但 URGENS 威胁要在我不知情的情况下向银行寄发关于我的匿名信，而他自己则逃离哈尔滨。我对此感到害怕，被迫同意继续签发支票。接下来的两张支票，编号分别为03295和03294，日期分别为10月24日和25日，我亲自在街上交给了 URGENS，因为他不再来银行，在这两张支票上，URGENS 伪造了 RUBANOVICH 账户持有人的签名，金额分别为3200日元和3100日元。上述支票的钱款也由 USHAKOFF 领取，我从 Urgens 处得到了4700日元现金，此外，为了掩人耳目，Ushakoff 欠我的300日元被退回到了 OKUN 的账户。在这次最后得逞后，URGENS 表示他将暂时停止支票交易并前往上海，还补充说 USHAKOFF 已经南下。12月，我收到 Urgens 从上海寄来的信，询问是否一切安好。我回信至上海霞飞路636号6室。此后再未见过 URGENS。Ushakoff 是否离开了哈尔滨，以及这是否是他的真名，我均不知情。但我能认出他。不久后，我遇到了银行前雇员 Grigory Vladimirovich LVOFF，他向我借款100日元，我答应第二天给他；同时，我向他详细讲述了经由我进行的支票交易，并邀请他加入我继续伪造支票。LVOFF 起初犹豫不决，但最终妥协，并表示他将亲自伪造支票上的签名，但会找人来领取钱款。过了一两天，具体记不清了，LVOF 给我打电话，约定在 Birjevaya 街和 Kitaiskaya 街的拐角处见面，他告诉我他找到了一个正准备与其安排事宜的人，并邀请我加入，但我拒绝了。当天晚上，LVOFF 来到我家，说他找到的人名叫 FRANTZ，此人同意通过伪造支票领取钱款。第二天，我带了一张由名为 POPEL 的账户持有人签名的卡片到 LVOFF 家，LVOFF 经过短暂练习后，第二天在我的房间里签署了支票。当时当场决定派人去银行领取这笔钱，此事以与之前相同的方式完成，即凭11月3日开具的第06267号支票，金额为5100金美元（美国货币）。钱款按当日汇率以日元支付，共计10836.65日元。当晚，LVOFF 将我的分成5000日元带到我家。LVOFF 随后告诉我，他不想再进行任何伪造，但那个名叫

page_data.en:
- 3 -

FRANTZ was forcing him to do it by means of threats to give
him away, etc. I also refused to take part in further such
activity. Later on FRANTZ had evidently decided to act on
his own, disregarding our wishes, and having obtained in the
Bank a reserve cheque, which he most probably filled in and
forged the signature of "Naftalin" himself (cheque No. 32257
dated November 23, 1928), which he presented for payment
to the Cashier. On checking the cheque was found by the
Cashier to be a rough imitation and was not paid out. The
bearer of the cheque in the meantime disappeared from the Bank.
This happened at the end of November last year. In this case
I came under the suspicion of the Bank and I confessed
everything to the Directors, mentioning LVOFF as accomplice
too. I will be able to identify FRANTZ also.
The total amount of my share from the monies received by means
of forged cheques came to 10.800 Yen. I spent 6113 Yen
(six thousand one hundred and eighteen) on the purchase in
different stores of silver table ware and other articles,
2000 Yen to pay the debts of my father-in-law, Alexander
Ivanovich ANDOGSKY on his promissory notes, 60 Yen to engraver
SARATOFF, Yamskaya No. 33 as a loan, 275 dol. to Doctor
FAVORSKY, Hotel "Eldorado", 60 dol. to Yakov Zikoff, 600
dollars to Mendrin, "Novy Mir" and 300 Yen sent to Russia.
The balance of 1387 Yen I spent on my personal wants and
in small sums here and there. The silver ware to the value
of 6118 Yen were kept by Yakov Zikoff and Doctor Favorsky,
who at the request of the Bank returned it to the latter.
In addition to that the Bank recovered some of its losses
by the 300 Yen paid in on the account of OKUN, my salary of
about 100 Yen, the Pension Fund sum of 50 Yen, about 950
Yen constituting the balance of my accounts in the Bank
and by the confiscation of my gold watch, which cost 150
Yen and which I bought in 1927. I have nothing more to add
in connection with the case. The statement has been read
out to me and is written correctly:
Sd. Alexander Alexandrovich CHULKOFF

Inspectors SOSIK, FEDOROFF.

The persons mentioned by me had nothing to do with the case
and they were not at all aware how I got the articles, which
they were keeping for me. These persons are Y. Zikoff, Y.M.
Favorsky, B.P. SARAPOFF and A.I. ANDOGSKY.
Sd. Alexander Alexandrovich CHULKOFF

January 25, 1929.
Inspectors SOSIK & FEDOROFF

Identical with the original:

Sd.
Chief Clerk of the Detective Department.
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

FRANTZ 的人通过威胁揭发他等手段强迫他继续做。我也拒绝参与进一步的此类活动。后来，FRANTZ 显然决定不顾我们的意愿单独行动，他在银行获得了一张备用支票，他很可能是自己填写并伪造了“Naftalin”的签名（1928年11月23日的第32257号支票），并将其提交给出纳付款。出纳在核对支票时发现这是拙劣的仿制品，因此未予支付。与此同时，持票人从银行消失。此事发生在去年11月底。在此案中，我受到了银行的怀疑，我向董事们坦白了一切，并提到 LVOFF 也是同伙。我也能认出 FRANTZ。
我通过伪造支票所得钱款中的分成总额为10,800日元。我花费6113日元（六千一百一十八）在不同商店购买银质餐具和其他物品，2000日元用于偿还岳父 Alexander Ivanovich ANDOGSKY 的本票债务，60日元作为贷款借给位于 Yamskaya 街33号的雕刻师 SARATOFF，275美元支付给住在“埃尔多拉多”酒店（Hotel "Eldorado"）的 FAVORSKY 医生，60美元给 Yakov Zikoff，600美元给“新世界”（"Novy Mir"）的 Mendrin，以及300日元汇往俄罗斯。剩余的1387日元我用于个人开销及零星支出。价值6118日元的银器由 Yakov Zikoff 和 Favorsky 医生保管，应银行要求，他们将其归还给了银行。此外，银行通过存入 OKUN 账户的300日元、我约100日元的薪水、50日元的养老金基金款项、构成我在银行账户余额的约950日元，以及没收我于1927年购买的价值150日元的金表，收回了部分损失。就此案而言，我无更多补充。笔录已向我宣读，记录无误：
签署：Alexander Alexandrovich CHULKOFF

督察 SOSIK, FEDOROFF。

我所提及的人员与本案无关，他们完全不知道我是如何获得由他们代为保管的物品的。这些人是 Y. Zikoff, Y.M. Favorsky, B.P. SARAPOFF 和 A.I. ANDOGSKY。
签署：Alexander Alexandrovich CHULKOFF

1929年1月25日。
督察 SOSIK & FEDOROFF

与原件一致：

签署：
侦探部首席书记员。

page_data.en:
G. J. Smith

* See D p.17/18

Statement of LVOFF, Grigory Vladimirovich,
22 years of age, Orthodox, no previous
conviction, married, Russian emigrant,
native of Moscow, residing at No. 25
Konnaya Street, Apt. I, on January 25:-

"I arrived in Harbin in 1920 as a refugee from Russia. I
have my mother, sister and two brothers here, who live at Modiagou,
Razdelnaya Street, No. 84. I have had fairly good education. In
the middle of 1926 I obtained employment at the "International
City" Bank on Kostivaya Street first as a watchman and later
was transferred to the office as a book-keeper in the Savings
Account Department. On August 25, 1928 I was dismissed for
being systematically late in coming to office and leaving it early.
Whilst employed I got married, which brought about expenses
difficult to meet. When already dismissed, in November of the
17th year of Chinese Republic, I requested Alexander CHULKOFF,
my ex colleague in the Bank's employ, to lend me 100 Yen, knowing
from his own story one day that he, together with some other
persons, obtained money from the Bank by means of forged cheques
on several occasions. CHULKOFF promised to let me have 100 Yen
the following day adding that he had an important matter to discuss
with me and will come to my house in consequence. The following
day CHULKOFF appeared at my house at 4 p.m. called me out and
said that he would obtain a card with the signature of one of
the owners of a Current Account as well as a blank cheque, which
I would have to fill in, forge the signature, and then find a
man who would present the cheque for payment. I consented to
that and began to look for a suitable man, but this took some
time when one fine day I was a visiting a friend Michail Andreevich
REPIN, at No. 36 Aptekarskaya Street, met in his rooms a man
named FRANTZ, but whose surname I never knew. Having left REPIN
together with FRANTZ the latter en route told me that he was out
of work and in straitened circumstances. I told FRANTZ about
the business which could be effected with the cheques and that
his task would only be to receive the money with a ready forged
cheque, to which FRANTZ consented. I told all this to CHULKOFF.
I think it was the same day CHULKOFF brought me a card with the
sample signature of one POPEL. After practicing for three days
the signature, I asked CHULKOFF to bring me the blan cheque, which
he did, handing it to me on the Kitaiskaya Street. The next day
at CHULKOFF's house I filled in the cheque and signed it "POPEL".
I then met FRANTZ on the Kitaiskaya Street and we both drove up
to the Bank. I stayed outside the Bank in the car, whilst FRANTZ
went in the Bank to receive the money. Having received the
receiving check we proceeded together to the Railway Administration
Office, from which we telephoned to CHULKOFF to ascertain that
everything was in order. The reply was satisfactory and we
returned to the Bank where again I waited outside in the car and
FRANTZ went in to present the check for payment of Cheque No.06267
dated 3/XI-28 to the amount of 5100 Gold Dollars, U.S.A. Currency
but the cash was given out in Yen at the day's rate of exchange.
Out of this money I took for myself 2200 Yen and gave CHULKOFF
5000. The rest of the money went to FRANTZ. I handed the money
to Chulkoff on the evening of the same day having called him out
in the corridor of his house. I spent the 2200 Yen. As regards
Cheque No. A.32257 with the forged signature of "Naftalin",
to the amount of 2100 Yen which FRANTZ failed to receive money for,
and who forged that cheque as well as how FRANTZ came into its
possession I do not know. I will be able to identify FRANTZ.
Concerning USHAKOFF I have never seen that man and do not know
who he is. I also do not know the whereabouts of both the
persons above mentioned. I have nothing more to add in connection
with the case. The statement has been read out to me and is
taken down correctly:
Sd. Grigory Vladimirovich LVOFF.
Inspectors FEDOROFF, SOSIK.

Identical with the original: Sd.
Chief Clerk of the Detective Depart
ment.
page_data.zh:
G. J. Smith

* 见 D 卷 第17/18页

LVOFF, Grigory Vladimirovich 的陈述，
22岁，东正教徒，无前科，已婚，俄国侨民，
莫斯科人，居住于马街（Konnaya Street）25号1室，1月25日陈述如下：

“我于1920年作为来自俄罗斯的难民抵达哈尔滨。我的母亲、姐姐和两个兄弟都在这里，居住在 Modiaogou（音译） Razdelnaya 街84号。我受过良好的教育。1926年中，我在 Kostivaya 街的‘国际城市’银行（"International City" Bank）受雇，起初担任看守，后来调至办公室储蓄账户部担任簿记员。1928年8月25日，我因系统性上班迟到和早退而被解雇。在职期间我结了婚，这带来了难以应付的开支。在被解雇后，即中华民国十七年十一月，我请求我在银行的前同事 Alexander CHULKOFF 借给我100日元，因为我曾听他讲述过，他与其他一些人曾多次通过伪造支票从银行获取资金。CHULKOFF 答应第二天给我100日元，并补充说他有一件重要事情要与我商量，因此会来我家。第二天下午4点，CHULKOFF 来到我家，把我叫出去，说他会弄来一张带有活期账户持有人之一签名的卡片以及一张空白支票，我需要填写、伪造签名，然后找一个去提示付款的人。我同意了，并开始寻找合适的人选，但这花了一些时间。直到有一天，我去拜访住在 Aptekarskaya 街36号的朋友 Michail Andreevich REPIN 时，在他房间里遇到了一个叫 FRANTZ 的人，但我从未知道他的姓氏。我和 FRANTZ 一起离开 REPIN 家，途中他告诉我他失业了，境况窘迫。我向 FRANTZ 介绍了可以通过支票进行的业务，他的任务仅仅是拿着伪造好的支票去领取钱款，FRANTZ 同意了。我将这一切告诉了 CHULKOFF。我想就是在那天，CHULKOFF 给我带来了一张印有 POPEL 签名样本的卡片。练习签名三天后，我让 CHULKOFF 给我拿来空白支票，他照做了，在 Kitaiskaya 街交给了我。第二天在 CHULKOFF 家，我填写了支票并签上了“POPEL”。随后我在 Kitaiskaya 街遇到 FRANTZ，我们两人乘车前往银行。我在银行外的车里等候，而 FRANTZ 进银行去领钱。拿到收款回执后，我们一起前往铁路管理局办公室，从那里打电话给 CHULKOFF 以确认一切正常。回复令人满意，我们返回银行，我再次在车外等候，FRANTZ 进去提示支付1928年11月3日开具的第06267号支票，金额为5100金美元（美国货币），但现金是按当日汇率以日元支付的。从这笔钱中，我拿了2200日元，给了 CHULKOFF 5000日元。剩余的钱归 FRANTZ。当晚，我在 CHULKOFF 家走廊把他叫出来，将钱交给了他。我花掉了这2200日元。至于带有伪造“Naftalin”签名的第 A.32257 号支票，金额为2100日元，FRANTZ 未能从中领到钱，该支票是谁伪造的以及 FRANTZ 是如何得到它的，我均不知情。我能认出 FRANTZ。关于 USHAKOFF，我从未见过此人，也不知道他是谁。我也不知道上述两人的下落。就此案而言，我无更多补充。笔录已向我宣读，记录无误：
签署：Grigory Vladimirovich LVOFF。
督察 FEDOROFF, SOSIK。

与原件一致：签署：
侦探部首席书记员。

page_data.en:
Statement of ZIKOFF, Yakov Yakovlevich,
Chinese Subject, 38 years of age,
Orthodox, no previous conviction,
residing at 16, Balkanskaya Street,
Kodiagou:-

"I am employed in the International Wagons Lits. I know
CHULKOFF, Alexander Alexandrovich since 1919 from the Military
School. I have always had the best opinion about Chulkoff
never suspecting him of being capable to be involved in an
unlawful affair of any kind and trusted him fully. I think it
was in October of last year that I bought, at the request of
CHULKOFF, a silver coffer for 2.200 dollars at a jewellers'
store, the money having been provided by him. I do not remember
the name of the store, but it is situated in Kitaiskaya Street.
Chulkoff said at the time that I would be able to buy that
piece of silver cheaper as he had already bargained for it
and could not get the price down. At the beginning of November
of last year, CHULKOFF handed me 5.500 Yen requesting that I
should place this money in the Bank in my own name because
being an employee of the Bank it was not right for him to place
much money in his own name as this might make the Bank suspicious
and will influence his employment. On being asked by me where
he got that much money from at all, Chulkoff replied that he
operated several successful commercial transactions. I thought
to myself that as Chulkoff has a father-in-law, who is in
financial difficulties, he probably does not wish his relatives
to know of his capital so that they should not ask for
assistance. I therefore consented and placed 5.500 Yen in
the City Bank in my own name, the money belonging to CHULKOFF.
Gradually CHULKOFF got that money out and only 10 Yen of his
remained outstanding in the book. On January 22, 1929 in the
evening CHULKOFF came to my house and requested me to take the
silver coffer, in my possession, to Dr. Favorsky's house, stating
that he has trouble at the Bank, after which he left. I tried
to ask him what had happened, but he was in a great hurry
and told me nothing. This coffer as I already said was bought
by me sometime in October of last year and was in my possession
at the request of CHULKOFF, who lived in a distant part of
town, rather isolated, and feared robbers. At the beginning of
December of last year CHULKOFF asked me to call at the
Engraver SARAPOFF's on the Yamskaya Street and take from him
his, CHULKOFF's silver ware, on which SARAPOFF was putting
his monograms. I called on SARAPOFF and he gave me the silverware.
CHULKOFF wanted the things to be in one place i.e. in my
possession. On January 23, 1929 I took the things over to
Dr. Favorsky. I confirm that I am not in any way connected
with the case and consider myself not only innocent of
complicity, but having been morally victimized for my trust
in CHULKOFF, who took advantage of it. The Bank, which
is the principal victim concerned in this case in the
person of its Manager, has also sent a letter to the International
Wagons Lits concerning my complete rehabilitation in this
case. I have not asked or had any compensation from CHULKOFF
for keeping safely his things and money and he only lent me
once 60 dollars to buy an overcoat. The statement has been
read out to me and is taken down correctly:-
Sd. Yakov Yakovlevich ZIKOFF
Inspectors BARANOFF, SOSIK, FEDOROFF

Identical with the original:- Signed

Chief Clerk of the Detective Department.
page_data.zh:
齐科夫（ZIKOFF），雅科夫·雅科夫列维奇，供词：
中国籍民，38岁，东正教徒，无前科，
居住于柯达沟（Kodiagou）巴尔干斯卡亚街16号：-

“我就职于国际卧铺车公司（International Wagons Lits）。我自1919年从军校时期起就认识丘尔科夫（CHULKOFF），亚历山大·亚历山德罗维奇。我对丘尔科夫一直评价很好，从未怀疑他有能力卷入任何非法事务，并且完全信任他。我想那是去年十月，应丘尔科夫的请求，我在一家珠宝店以2,200美元购买了一个银箱，钱由他提供。我不记得那家店的名字，但它位于基泰斯卡亚街（Kitaiskaya Street）。丘尔科夫当时说，我可以更便宜地买到这件银器，因为他已经讲过价但无法再压低价格。去年十一月初，丘尔科夫交给我5,500日元，请求我以我自己的名义将这笔钱存入银行，因为作为银行职员，他以自己的名义存放大量资金是不合适的，这可能会引起银行的怀疑并影响他的工作。当我问他究竟从哪里得到这么多钱时，丘尔科夫回答说他是通过几笔成功的商业交易获得的。我心想，既然丘尔科夫有一位陷入财务困境的岳父，他可能不希望亲戚知道他的资本，以免他们请求资助。因此我同意了，并以我自己的名义将5,500日元存入城市银行（City Bank），这笔钱属于丘尔科夫。后来丘尔科夫逐渐取出了那笔钱，账面上只余下他的10日元。1929年1月22日晚，丘尔科夫来到我家，请求我将由我保管的银箱送到法沃尔斯基（Favorsky）医生家，称他在银行遇到了麻烦，随后便离开了。我试图问他发生了什么事，但他非常匆忙，什么也没告诉我。如前所述，这个箱子是我去年十月某个时候购买的，应丘尔科夫的要求由我保管，因为他住在城里一个遥远且相当偏僻的地方，害怕强盗。去年十二月初，丘尔科夫让我去扬姆斯卡亚街（Yamskaya Street）的雕刻师萨拉波夫（SARAPOFF）那里，取回他（丘尔科夫）的银器，萨拉波夫正在上面刻他的姓名缩写。我去拜访了萨拉波夫，他给了我那些银器。丘尔科夫希望这些东西放在一个地方，即由我保管。1929年1月23日，我将这些东西送到了法沃尔斯基医生处。我确认我与本案没有任何关联，并认为我不仅没有共犯之罪，反而因信任被丘尔科夫利用而在道德上成为了受害者。作为本案主要受害方的银行，其经理也已致函国际卧铺车公司，证明我在本案中完全清白。我没有因妥善保管他的物品和金钱而向丘尔科夫索取或获得任何报酬，他只曾借给我60美元买一件大衣。本供词已向我宣读，记录无误：-
签署：雅科夫·雅科夫列维奇·齐科夫
督察员：巴拉诺夫（BARANOFF）、索西克（SOSIK）、费多罗夫（FEDOROFF）

与原件一致：签署

侦探部首席书记员。

page_data.en:
Statement of Doctor Favorsky, Yakov
Mihailovich, 45 years of age, Orthodox,
no previous conviction, Russian emigrant,
native of Petrograd, residing at the
Hotel "Eldorado" Room No. 2, on Uchastkovaya
Street, on January 26, 1929:

"I have known CHULKOFF, Alexander Alexandrovich, since
March 1927, when he first came to me as a patient. I was
treating CHULKOFF for a period of 8 months and he remained
owing me a minimum sum of 275 dollars. At the end of May
1928, CHULKOFF having completed the treatment asked me to
wait for the payment of the money he owed as he was about to
get married and needed the money. In November last CHULKOFF
came back to me as a patient to check the state of his health.
At that time I reminded him of his debt when he said that
he would bring that same day a cheque of the International
Bank for the sum owing. Right enough CHULKOFF brought me
the cheque on that day which was signed by Y. ZIKOFF
and which on presentation on the following day at the Bank
was paid out. I do not know who ZIKOFF is. I do not quite
remember the date, but about five days ago, an unknown young
man brought me with a visiting card of CHULKOFF two locked
cases which were left with me for safe keeping. On the eve
of that day CHULKOFF called on me and requested that I should
take for safe keeping two cases, which he said contained
silverware and in view of the fact that he changed house
and was living in an isolated district near the Lopato factory,
he was afraid of robbers. I believed CHULKOFF and accepted
the silver for safe keeping. On the same day in the evening
two unknown men with Chulkoff's visiting card, herewith
enclosed, came to my house and asked for the silver, which
he instructed me to deliver and which I did. I knew absolutely
nothing about any unlawful and shady affairs of CHULKOFF.
CHULKOFF's statement that he loaned me 275 dollars is
incorrect.

Sd. FAVORSKY.

Additional Statement of Alexander
Alexandrovich CHULKOFF.

"From March 1927 I suffered from inflammation of the
kidneys and was really treated by Dr. Favorsky for about a
period of 8 months. In November of last year, I do not
remember the date, not feeling quite well I again went to
see Dr. Favorsky, who reminded me of my debt to him for the
previous treatment. I asked Favorsky how much I owed him
and he having told me the sum of 275 dollars I brought Dr.
Favorsky the same evening a cheque of the City Bank for the
sum of 275 dollars signed by Y. ZIKOFF. At the beginning of
November of last year I gave ZIKOFF, Yakov Yakovlevich,
5.500 Yen asking him as a friend to place this sum of money
in the City Bank on his own name. When asked by ZIKOFF
where did I get such a large sum of money and why did I
want it to put in the Bank in his, ZIKOFF's, name I answered
that I got the money through commercial transactions and
that I could not place it in my own name, because the Bank
might become suspicious as to where I got it, being such
a big sum. ZIKOFF believed me and placed the money in his
own name in the City Bank. Gradually I got the money out
leaving but 10 Yen marked on the book. ZIKOFF consented
to put the money in the Bank in his own name without any
compensation and only once asked me to lend him 60 dollars
in a friendly way to buy a coat. Zikoff at my request
a few days ago took two cases containing silverware for
safe keeping to Dr. Favorsky with my visiting card and on
the eve I personally requested Dr. Favorsky for permission
page_data.zh:
法沃尔斯基（FAVORSKY）医生，雅科夫·米哈伊洛维奇，供词：
45岁，东正教徒，无前科，俄国侨民，
彼得格勒人，居住于乌恰斯特科瓦亚街（Uchastkovaya Street）
“埃尔多拉多”酒店（Hotel "Eldorado"）2号房间，
1929年1月26日：

“我自1927年3月起认识丘尔科夫（CHULKOFF），亚历山大·亚历山德罗维奇，当时他首次作为病人来找我。我为丘尔科夫治疗了8个月，他至今仍欠我至少275美元。1928年5月底，丘尔科夫完成治疗后，请求我暂缓支付他所欠的款项，因为他即将结婚，需要这笔钱。去年十一月，丘尔科夫再次作为病人来找我看病，检查健康状况。当时我提醒他尚欠债务，他说当天就会带来一张国际银行（International Bank）的支票以支付欠款。果然，丘尔科夫当天给我带来了支票，由Y.齐科夫（Y. ZIKOFF）签署，次日在银行提示付款时得以兑付。我不认识齐科夫是谁。我不太记得确切日期，但大约五天前，一个陌生的年轻人拿着丘尔科夫的名片给我送来两个上锁的手提箱，委托我代为保管。在那天的前一天晚上，丘尔科夫拜访了我，请求我代为保管两个手提箱，他说里面装有银器，鉴于他搬了家，住在拉帕托（Lopato）工厂附近的一个偏僻地区，他担心遭遇强盗。我相信了丘尔科夫，接受了这些银器代为保管。同一天晚上，两名手持丘尔科夫名片（附后）的陌生男子来到我家，要求提取银器，这是丘尔科夫指示我交付的，我也照办了。我对丘尔科夫的任何非法和可疑勾当绝对一无所知。丘尔科夫声称借给我275美元的说法是不正确的。

签署：法沃尔斯基（FAVORSKY）。

亚历山大·亚历山德罗维奇·丘尔科夫（CHULKOFF）的补充供词。

“自1927年3月起，我患有肾炎，确实由法沃尔斯基医生治疗了约8个月。去年十一月，我不记得具体日期，因感觉身体不适，我又去看法沃尔斯基医生，他提醒我此前治疗所欠的债务。我问法沃尔斯基我欠他多少钱，他告诉我是275美元，当晚我便给法沃尔斯基医生带去了一张由Y.齐科夫签署的城市银行（City Bank）支票，金额为275美元。去年十一月初，我交给雅科夫·雅科夫列维奇·齐科夫5,500日元，请他作为朋友以他自己的名义将这笔钱存入城市银行。当齐科夫问我从哪里得到这么大一笔钱，以及为什么我想以他（齐科夫）的名义存入银行时，我回答说这笔钱是通过商业交易获得的，我不能以自己的名义存放，因为数额如此之大，可能会引起银行对资金来源的怀疑。齐科夫相信了我，并以他自己的名义将钱存入了城市银行。后来我逐渐取出了这笔钱，账面上只留下10日元。齐科夫同意以他自己的名义将钱存入银行，未收取任何报酬，仅曾有一次以朋友身份向我借款60美元购买大衣。几天前，应我的请求，齐科夫拿着我的名片，将两个装有银器的手提箱送到法沃尔斯基医生处代为保管，并在前一天晚上，我亲自请求法沃尔斯基医生允许

page_data.en:
- 2 -

to place in his house for safe keeping 2 cases with silver
ware explaining that I changed house to a distant part of
town, not far from the Lppato factory and was afraid of
robbers, and Dr. Favorsky agreed to accept the things. In
the evening of the same day I gave my visiting card, at the
request of the Manager of the Bank, who detained me, with
the request that my things should be delivered by Dr. Favorsky
to bearers from the Bank, and this was done, the things
having been brought to the Bank. In my first statement
I said that I just gave Dr. Favorsky 275 dollars. I made such
a statement only because I did not want to confide in the
Authorities that I was ill, considering that this concerns
me only and not the case in connection with which I am detained.
I really paid Dr. FAVORSKY the 275 dollars for his treatment
of me in illness.

The statement has been read out:
Jc. Alexander Alexandrovich CHULKOFF.

Inspectors SOSIK, FEDOROFF.

Identical with the original.    Signed.

Chief Clerk of the Detective
Department.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

将两个装有银器的手提箱放在他家中代为保管，解释说我搬到了城里远离市中心、离拉帕托（Lppato）工厂不远的一个偏僻地方，担心遭遇强盗，法沃尔斯基医生同意接收这些物品。当天晚上，应扣留我的银行经理的要求，我交出了我的名片，请求法沃尔斯基医生将我的物品交付给来自银行的持票人，此事已办妥，物品已被送往银行。在我第一次供词中，我说我只是给了法沃尔斯基医生275美元。我之所以那样陈述，是因为我不想向当局透露我生病的事，认为这仅与我个人有关，与我被拘留所涉的案件无关。我确实支付了法沃尔斯基（FAVORSKY）医生275美元，作为他为我治病的费用。

供词已宣读：
签署：亚历山大·亚历山德罗维奇·丘尔科夫。

督察员：索西克（SOSIK）、费多罗夫（FEDOROFF）。

与原件一致。    签署。

侦探部
首席书记员。

page_data.en:
Statement of YASTREMSKY, IVAN
Nikolaevich, 34 years of age,
Orthodox, no previous conviction,
Married, Russian emigrant, Native of
Slaviansk, Harkhov Province, residing
at No. I Vagonnaya Street, apt. I :

" USHAKOFF is my wife's brother. Our mutual relations
have always been strained owing to his refusing to work.
Ushakoff very seldom paid visits to my house and these he did
when I was out at work, driving a motor bus. I know absolutely
nothing about Ushakoff's forged cheque transactions. I do not
even know exactly where Ushakoff resided recently in Harbin,
but possibly he put up at the Hotel "Central". In November
of last year, Ushakoff dropped in when I was engaged repairing
a motor car in the garage, to say good bye and told me that
he was leaving for the South to try his luck, and at the
request of my wife I lent him 50 dollars for travelling
expenses. Four or five days later we received a letter
from Ushakoff, which has already been submitted. Neither
my wife or I know anything about the alleged offence
committed by Ushakoff. I do not know Ushakoff's friends
Lvoff, Grigory, or Chuikoff, Alexander. I have no more to
add to this statement. The statement has been read out
to me and is taken down correctly:

Sd. Ivan Yastremsky.

Inspectors SOSIK, FEDOROFF, BARANOFF

Remark: A telegram dated 29/I/-18 year of the Chinese Republic
was sent to Shanghai to detain USHAKOFF

Inspector SOSIK.

Identical with the original: Signed

Chief Clerk of the Detective Department.
page_data.zh:
雅斯特雷姆斯基（YASTREMSKY），伊万·尼古拉耶维奇，供词：
34岁，东正教徒，无前科，
已婚，俄国侨民，哈尔科夫省斯拉维扬斯克（Slaviansk）人，
居住于瓦贡纳亚街（Vagonnaya Street）1号1室：

“乌沙科夫（USHAKOFF）是我妻子的兄弟。由于他拒绝工作，我们之间的关系一直很紧张。乌沙科夫很少来我家拜访，而且都是在我外出驾驶公共汽车工作时来的。我对乌沙科夫伪造支票的交易绝对一无所知。我甚至不知道乌沙科夫最近在哈尔滨的确切住址，但他可能住在‘中央’酒店（Hotel "Central"）。去年十一月，乌沙科夫在我于车库修理汽车时顺道来访，向我告别，并告诉我他将去南方碰碰运气，应我妻子的请求，我借给他50美元作为旅费。四五天之后，我们收到了乌沙科夫的一封信，该信已提交。我和我妻子对乌沙科夫涉嫌犯下的罪行均一无所知。我不认识乌沙科夫的朋友利沃夫（Lvoff）、格里戈里（Grigory）或丘伊科夫（Chuikoff），亚历山大。对此供词我无更多补充。本供词已向我宣读，记录无误：

签署：伊万·雅斯特雷姆斯基。

督察员：索西克（SOSIK）、费多罗夫（FEDOROFF）、巴拉诺夫（BARANOFF）

备注：一份日期为中华民国十七年（1928年）1月29日的电报已发往上海，要求拘留乌沙科夫（USHAKOFF）

督察员：索西克（SOSIK）。

与原件一致：签署

侦探部首席书记员。

Statement of 3 K.OFF Gavril, 45
years of age, no previous conviction,
citizen of R. S. F. S. R. Orthodox, residing
at No. 33 Yamskaya Street:-

"I am an engraver and jeweller by profession and possess
a jewellery shop in the house in which I live. Chulkoff, Alexan-
der Alexandrovich has been my customer since 1925. On several
occasions, at Chulkoff's request, I visited Mr. Campi's jewellery
shop in Nizhegorodskaya street, in which the Hotel Lucerne is
situated, to examine several silver objects previously chosen
by Chulkoff, for the purpose of appraising their value. In
October last, I cannot give the exact date, Mr. Chulkoff brought
a little silver box and was accompanied by a man whom he
introduced to me as his friend, Yukoff, Yakov Yakovlevich. At
Chulkoff's request I examined the silver box and the quality
of the jewels which it bore. 15 or 20 minutes later Mr. Chulkoff
together with Yukoff took this silver box away. At that time
I had several orders placed by Mr. Chulkoff. Early in December
of last year, by order of Chulkoff, I handed over all the silver
belonging to him to Mr. Yukoff, who came to my shop and took
all these things away with him. I do not know nor was I
interested to know where he had taken these articles to. Mr.
Chulkoff was my regular customer, whom I esteemed as such
believing him to be a rich man, all the more so as Chulkoff
himself told me he was a person of distinction and I engraved
a crown on several of his objects, which was proof of his being
a distinguished person. I never discussed with Chulkoff his
personal affairs nor the means by which he earned his money. In
addition Mr. Chulkoff always addressed me as customers are in
the habit of doing.
The statement has been read out to me and is taken down
correctly:
M. Gavril Sarapoff

Inspectors A.K.OFF, A. OEFF.

Statement of ANDREEV, Alexander
Ivanovich, 52 years of age, Orthodox,
married, Russian emigrant, born in
Novgorod, residing at Rochotnaya Street,
No. 108, apt. 5. :-

"I knew Mr. Chulkoff, Alexander Alexandrovich several years
before he married my daughter. In the spring of 1927 Mr.
Chulkoff, on his arrival from Korea, where he was employed in
a foreign mining company, renewed his acquaintance with my
family and then married my daughter in February 1928. It
was known to me that upon his arrival from Korea he had
savings amounting to 3 or 5 thousand dollars; this, however, I wish
to state, was my own personal estimation of his savings as
he had been earning 300 yen per month in Korea during four
years and had lived very economically. After my daughter's
marriage I gave her a present of 50 American dollars. Only
in October last I was urgently pressed to redeem a bill due
to the Bank of the Society of House Owners amounting to 150
dollars, local currency. Having no means to redeem this debt
I approached my son-in-law Chulkoff with the request either
to loan me the above sum through the intermediary of his
banking acquaintances or to return me temporarily the monetary
wedding present of my daughter. Mr. Chulkoff complied with
my request and redeemed my bill of exchange. I cannot say
where he obtained the money for this purpose, but I had the
impression that he got out of the money I gave my daughter
at her wedding. There was, however, an instance when Chulkoff
page_data.zh:
K.OFF 警员加夫里尔（Gavril）的陈述，45岁，无前科，俄罗斯苏维埃联邦社会主义共和国公民，东正教徒，居住于亚姆斯卡亚街（Yamskaya Street）33号：-

“我是一名雕刻师和珠宝商，在我居住的房子里拥有一家珠宝店。亚历山大·亚历山德罗维奇·丘尔科夫（Chulkoff, Alexander Alexandrovich）自1925年以来一直是我的顾客。应丘尔科夫的请求，我曾数次前往下诺夫哥罗德街（Nizhegorodskaya street）坎皮（Campi）先生的珠宝店（卢塞恩酒店即位于此），查验丘尔科夫先前选定的几件银器，以评估其价值。去年十月，具体日期我已无法回忆，丘尔科夫先生带来一个小银盒，并陪同一名他向我介绍为其朋友的男子，即雅科夫·雅科夫列维奇·尤科夫（Yukoff, Yakov Yakovlevich）。应丘尔科夫的请求，我检查了该银盒及其所镶嵌宝石的质量。15或20分钟后，丘尔科夫先生与尤科夫一同将该银盒带走。当时，我有几笔由丘尔科夫先生下达的订单。去年十二月初，按照丘尔科夫的命令，我将属于他的所有银器移交给来到我店里的尤科夫先生，后者将所有这些物品带走。我不知道，也不感兴趣知道他将这些物品带往何处。丘尔科夫先生是我的常客，我视其为富人而尊重他，尤其是因为丘尔科夫本人告诉我他是一位显贵人士，且我在他的几件物品上雕刻了皇冠，这证明了他是一位显贵。我从未与丘尔科夫讨论过他的个人事务或其赚钱的手段。此外，丘尔科夫先生总是像顾客习惯做的那样与我交谈。
本陈述已向我宣读，记录无误：
M. 加夫里尔·萨拉波夫（Gavril Sarapoff）

督察 A.K.OFF，A. OEFF。

安德烈耶夫（ANDREEV），亚历山大·伊万诺维奇的陈述，52岁，东正教徒，已婚，俄国流亡者，出生于诺夫哥罗德，居住于罗霍特纳亚街（Rochotnaya Street）108号5室：-

“在丘尔科夫，亚历山大·亚历山德罗维奇娶我女儿之前几年，我就认识他。1927年春，丘尔科夫从朝鲜归来，他在那里受雇于一家外国矿业公司，重新与我家建立联系，并于1928年2月娶了我的女儿。据我所知，他从朝鲜归来时拥有3000至5000美元的储蓄；然而，我要声明，这是我对他储蓄的个人估算，因为他在朝鲜四年间每月赚取300日元，且生活非常节俭。女儿婚后，我送给她50美元作为礼物。直到去年十月，我才被迫切需兑付一张欠房东协会银行（Bank of the Society of House Owners）的票据，金额为150元本地货币。由于无力偿还这笔债务，我请求女婿丘尔科夫要么通过他的银行熟人 intermediary 借给我上述款项，要么暂时归还我女儿的结婚礼金。丘尔科夫答应了我的请求，兑付了我的汇票。我说不出他是从哪里弄到这笔钱的，但我印象中他是从我在女儿婚礼上给她的钱中拿出来的。不过，有一次丘尔科夫

page_data.en:
bought a Victrola, and I asked him how he could afford to
spend such a sum of money out of his salary of 120 Yen per
month. Chulkoff replied that he happened to earn some money
through speculation on currency exchange. I partly believed
his explanation because I considered that he had still some
savings left from his stay in Korea. Chulkoff paid me out of
his salary received from the Bank $60 monthly for his and his
wife's board and lodging. I knew absolutely nothing of
Chulkoff's unlawful transactions with forged cheques nor did
I know that he was buying valuable silver tea sets and other
things. I have never seen him to have such things in my house
and he never told me of having bought them. I consider it
necessary to add that Chulkoff redeemed other bills amounting
to 500 Rls, contracted by us jointly. Chulkoff never lent
me a large sum of money nor did he borrow same. I have nothing
more to add to the foregoing.
The statement has been read out to me and is taken down
correctly.
(sgd.) Alexander Ivanovich Andogsky.

Inspectors JOSIK, PHNOKOFF
page_data.zh:
买了一台维克多留声机（Victrola），我问他怎么能用每月120日元的薪水花这么多钱。丘尔科夫回答说，他碰巧通过外汇投机赚了一些钱。我部分相信他的解释，因为我认为他在朝鲜期间还剩下一些积蓄。丘尔科夫每月从他在银行获得的薪水中支付60美元，作为他和妻子的食宿费。我对丘尔科夫涉及伪造支票的非法交易一无所知，也不知道他正在购买昂贵的银茶具和其他物品。我从未在他家里见过此类物品，他也从未告诉过我他购买了这些东西。我认为有必要补充一点，丘尔科夫兑付了我们共同承担的另外价值500卢布的票据。丘尔科夫从未借给我大笔款项，我也未向他借款。对此我没有更多要补充的了。
本陈述已向我宣读，记录无误。
（签名）亚历山大·伊万诺维奇·安多格斯基（Alexander Ivanovich Andogsky）。

督察 JOSIK，PHNOKOFF
