COPY
Harbin, Manchuria,
January 23rd, 1929.

CONFESSION OF CHULKOFF.

THE START:
I was talking with Ivoff who spoke of how easy it is to get money from the Bank from forged checks. We discussed how easy it would be to copy the signatures say on a check from a book just issued. He said that if a check from a customer's check book could be obtained and the signature forged it would go through easily and the Bank would not accept responsibility. Even a counter check if the signature was correct could be safely cashed providing the forgery was good enough. At that time nothing more was said. That was about in July or August.

We discussed the possibility of securing money in this way but arranged nothing definite up to the time Ivoff left. We thought that as Clark was new and inexperienced, with too much work to check up things carefully that such a plan would succeed. Young was much more careless; he would sign anything without any particular attention. But he was only there for 1½ months after I joined the Bank and before we discussed this way of getting money.

I kept thinking about what Ivoff and I had talked and felt tempted to get some money as it was urgently needed at home, where my father-in-law sold everything to pay back the money he took (about Loc.$5,000.-).

A man came from Shanghai by the name of Vladimir Micho-laevitch Yurgens about September. His address is Ave. Joffre No. 636, Apartment 6, Shanghai where he is probably now. I knew him in Vladivostock in 1922 - or rather 1923 and became quite good friends with him.

I met Yurgens on the street and went with him to a cafe but did not take him home.

He told me that he was desperately in need of money and would do anything to get that money. I told him I was working in a Bank.

A few days later, by appointment we met again and he told me about instances of getting money from Banks and he had been in our Bank and saw our system. He suggested that we could get some money out of the Bank, a few thousand (he needed about H.$ 10,000) and I had been thinking it over and decided that we might try. I didn't want to try too large a sum as I thought we would be caught and I didn't wish to take any risk. I agreed and explained how it could be done.

Anyone could apply for and receive a counter check. Then I could get the signature card, we could fill the check on an account, whose balance was known. He agreed to do the forgery and fill in the check but he said that he couldn't come to get the money personally as he was known in the city and might be recognised. He said, however, that he would send a man and I asked who. He said his name was Ushakov, who lived on Commercial Street. He said the man would leave the town afterwards so that he would not betray us. We discussed who it could be and picked out two rich Jews - Okun and Rubanovitch.

We found that Okun had Yen 3,000.- in his account and Rubanovitch about US$1,000. So we decided to start with Yen 300. Yurgens came and got a counter check from Maitz. The same day I took out the signature card after 1 p.m. and gave it to Yurgens that afternoon. Next morning at 8.05 in Newtown he met me by appointment and gave back the signature card and showed me the check the forged signature looked very good to me and we arranged that
page_data.zh:
副本
满洲，哈尔滨，
1929年1月23日。

丘尔科夫的供认。

开端：
我与伊沃夫（Ivoff）交谈，他谈到从银行通过伪造支票获取资金是多么容易。我们讨论了复制刚发出的支票簿上的签名是多么容易。他说，如果能弄到客户支票簿中的一张支票并伪造签名，就能顺利兑现，银行也不会承担责任。即使是柜台支票，只要签名正确，且伪造得足够好，也可以安全兑现。当时没有再多说什么。那大约是在七月或八月。

我们讨论了以这种方式获取资金的可能性，但在伊沃夫离开之前并未做出任何具体安排。我们认为，由于克拉克（Clark）是新来的，缺乏经验，工作繁忙无暇仔细核查，这样的计划会成功。扬（Young）则更加粗心；他会不加特别注意地签署任何文件。但他在我加入银行后仅待了一个半月，在我们讨论这种搞钱方法之前他就离开了。

我一直在思考我和伊沃夫的谈话，并感到诱惑去弄些钱，因为家里急需用钱，我的岳父变卖了一切来偿还他借走的钱（约本地货币5,000元）。

大约在九月，一个叫弗拉基米尔·米哈伊洛维奇·尤尔根斯（Vladimir Micho-laevitch Yurgens）的人从上海来到此地。他的地址是上海霞飞路（Ave. Joffre）636号6室，他现在可能还住在那里。我于1922年——或者更确切地说是1923年——在海参崴认识他，并成为了相当好的朋友。

我在街上遇到尤尔根斯，和他一起去了一家咖啡馆，但没有带他回家。

他告诉我他极度缺钱，愿意做任何事来搞到钱。我告诉他我在一家银行工作。

几天后，我们按约定再次见面，他讲述了从银行获取资金的案例，并表示他曾来过我们银行，了解我们的系统。他建议我们可以从银行弄出一些钱，几千块（他需要约港币10,000元），我经过考虑，决定我们可以试试。我不想尝试太大的金额，因为我认为我们会被抓，我也不想承担任何风险。我同意了，并解释了如何操作。

任何人都可以申请并领取柜台支票。然后我可以取出签名卡，我们在一个余额已知的账户上填写支票。他同意进行伪造并填写支票，但他说他不能亲自来取钱，因为他在城里有人认识，可能会被认出来。不过他说他会派一个人来，我问是谁。他说那人叫乌沙科夫（Ushakov），住在商业街（Commercial Street）。他说那人之后会离开这座城市，这样就不会出卖我们。我们讨论了目标人选，挑中了两个富有的犹太人——奥昆（Okun）和鲁巴诺维奇（Rubanovitch）。

我们发现奥昆的账户里有3,000日元，鲁巴诺维奇约有1,000美元。所以我们决定先从300日元开始。尤尔根斯来并从梅茨（Maitz）那里拿到了一张柜台支票。同一天下午1点后，我取出了签名卡，并在当天下午交给了尤尔根斯。第二天早上8点05分，他在新城（Newtown）按约定与我见面，交还了签名卡，并给我看了那张支票，伪造的签名在我看来非常好，我们商定

page_data.en:
his man should come to the Bank and I would give him a brass
check for the forged check and then he should go out of the Bank.
In case the check was found forged I was to notify Yurgens when
he called me up on the phone. I was so disturbed that I even
forgot to have Ushakov endorse the check. Yurgens called me up
in 15 minutes and I replied that "my health was good" which meant
that the check is O.K. and he must send Ushakov in to get the
money. He came and got it but I did not watch for him nor see
him.

We were elated over this and decided to try again.
I remember watching Clark when he compared the first signature
and he hesitated a little but passed it.

This time I had received Yen 100.- Yurgens took Yen
200.- to divide with Ushakov.

On the 16th October we had another meeting and as
everything had gone well we decided to do it again for a bigger
amount. So on the 17th Yurgens got another counter check and I
gave him the signature card again in the afternoon. The next
morning he showed me the forged check, which I found O.K. and I
replaced the signature card when Clark was busy at the counter.
Ushakov came again and we followed the same procedure, obtaining
Yen 2,700.- of which Ushakov, as Yurgens said, had received Yen
700. He kept Yen 1,000 for himself and gave me Yen 1,000.

I had already used up the Yen 100.- in paying bills
at Petroff's, a grocery store, Armies etc. With the Yen 1,000.-
which I had in my pocket, I bought in a few days a $30.- tea
spoon, fork and tongs at Itzikson's and deposited Yen 300.- back
to Okun's account, with no good reason for doing so except that
I had too much money. I gave my wife Yen 800.- and told her to
deposit the money to her account in the Thrift Corporation. She
asked where the money came from as we had never had any before
and wanted to open a joint account and I told here that I made the
money by speculating on currencies. She believed me and took the
money there. I made a mistake in saying that I deposited Yen 300.-
out of the cash in my pocket to Okun's account. That came later.

Yurgens came again and said that we must do it again.
I refused to join him and said if he wanted to he could do it on
his own account. We quarrelled. He came again and said that
if I refused to do it he would write a letter to certain people
and would clear out of town himself. Thereupon I agreed to do it
again. He told me to find out the balance of Rabinovitch, which
I got from the weekly balance book. Yurgens said he would not
come to the Bank himself, but told me to get two counter checks
in U.S.$, which I did on the following day. I gave them to him
with the signature card, which he returned to me on the following
morning and showed me two checks not yet filled in except for
the forged signatures. I said I didn't like one and wanted to
destroy it but he wouldn't give it to me. I told him to put
U.S.$3,000.- on one which was to be the last one.

The same day Ushakov came to the Bank and presented
two checks, one for G.$3,100.- and one for U.S.$3,200.- to me.
I asked Tsizik to give him numbers for the checks which he did.
I calculated the amount of Yen and asked Mailitz to write out
the contract. I laid the check and contract on Clark's desk.
Clark examined the signatures on both checks and then personally
looked at the balance in the ledger. Then he initialled them
and they went through. Yurgens telephoned again and I gave the
usual reply. Ushakov came and got the money.

We met, Yurgens and I, after 1 p.m. and I got Yen 5,000
On the same day I deposited Yen 300.- to Okun's account so as to
make the check for Yen 300.- look correct. Within a few days say
about a week my wife and I were walking by Kaspe's and saw the sil
page_data.zh:
他的人应该来银行，我会给他一个铜牌以换取那张伪造的支票，然后他离开银行。万一发现支票是伪造的，我会在尤尔根斯打电话给我时通知他。我当时非常紧张，甚至忘了让乌沙科夫在支票上背书。尤尔根斯在15分钟后给我打电话，我回答说“我身体很好”，这意味着支票没问题，他必须派乌沙科夫进去取钱。乌沙科夫来了并取走了钱，但我没有盯着他，也没看见他。

我们为此感到兴奋，并决定再试一次。
我记得观察克拉克核对第一个签名时，他犹豫了一下，但还是通过了。

这次我得到了100日元。尤尔根斯拿了200日元与乌沙科夫平分。

10月16日，我们再次会面，鉴于一切顺利，我们决定再做一次，金额更大。因此，17日尤尔根斯又拿到了一张柜台支票，我再次在下午将签名卡交给他。第二天早上，他给我看了伪造的支票，我觉得没问题，趁克拉克在柜台忙碌时，我换回了签名卡。乌沙科夫又来了，我们遵循同样的程序，获得了2,700日元，其中据尤尔根斯说，乌沙科夫得到了700日元。尤尔根斯自己留下了1,000日元，给了我1,000日元。

我已经用那100日元在彼得罗夫（Petroff）杂货店、军队等地支付了账单。用我口袋里的1,000日元，我在几天内于伊齐克森（Itzikson）店里购买了一套价值30美元的茶匙、叉子和夹子，并将300日元存回奥昆的账户，这样做除了因为我钱太多外没有别的正当理由。我给了妻子800日元，让她把钱存入节俭公司（Thrift Corporation）的账户。她问钱是从哪里来的，因为我们以前从未有过这么多钱，她想开一个联合账户，我告诉她我是通过货币投机赚的钱。她相信了我，把钱存到了那里。我说我从口袋里的现金中拿出300日元存入奥昆的账户，这是一个错误。那是后来发生的。

尤尔根斯又来了，说我们必须再做一次。我拒绝参与，并说如果他想做，可以自己做。我们吵了一架。他又来了，说如果我拒绝做，他就会给某些人写信，并自己离开这座城市。于是我又同意再做一次。他让我查明拉比诺维奇（Rabinovitch）的余额，我从每周余额簿中查到了。尤尔根斯说他不会亲自来银行，而是让我拿两张美元柜台支票，我在第二天照办了。我把支票和签名卡交给他，他在第二天早上还给我，并给我看了两张除了伪造签名外尚未填写的支票。我说我不喜欢其中一张，想销毁它，但他不肯给我。我让他在那张将是最后一张的支票上填上3,000美元。

同一天，乌沙科夫来到银行，向我出示了两张支票，一张为3,100金马克（G.$），另一张为3,200美元。我请齐齐克（Tsizik）给他支票号码，他照办了。我计算了日元金额，并请梅利茨（Mailitz）写出合约。我把支票和合约放在克拉克的桌子上。克拉克检查了两张支票上的签名，然后亲自查看了分类账中的余额。然后他草签了字，支票便通过了。尤尔根斯又打来电话，我给出了惯常的回答。乌沙科夫来取走了钱。

下午1点后，我和尤尔根斯见面，我得到了5,000日元。同一天，我向奥昆的账户存入了300日元，以便使那张300日元的支票看起来正确。几天后，大约一周左右，我和妻子路过卡斯佩（Kaspe）家时，看到了那套银

page_data.en:
silver jewel box. We had gone inside to buy a watch for my
wife. While buying the watch I enquired the price of the box.
He said Loc.$1,800. I said it was too much and we went out,
after having bought watch for my wife for Mex $300. I did not
pay for it or take it, no, I remember I did pay for it and the next
day my wife came to take it. On the same evening when we bought the
watch, I told my wife we could buy the silver box. I sent a man
named Sarapov, who lives on Yamskaya St., and who has done many
things for me engravings etc. to buy the box for me. Sarapov is
in no way connected with this forgery business. He bought it for
Yen 1,200.- and I asked Sarapov to keep it for me.

Then I wanted to buy something else as we never had
anything pretty in our house. I had explained to my wife that I
got the money by speculations on currencies.

So we went again to Kuspe's and asked if he had
silverware. We looked at the silver sets and agreed to buy one
for Yen 2,000. I said I would send my man who would pay for it.
I gave Sarapov Yen 2,000 and he got the silver set which he en-
graved for me. One half of it he engraved for me, but he did it
so badly, I had Lipkovsky do the balance of engraving. Lipkovsky
knows me and then he started talking that I had a lot of money and
I explained that I did it by trading with agents in Japan. The
silver set is engraved with my own initials and was kept at Zykoffs
but last night I went to Zykoff's and asked him to take it to the
Hotel Eldorado, and leave them with Mr. Favorsky, who I came to
know when I was living at that hotel and he took care of me when
I was ill. Please do not mix him up with this as he knows abso-
lutely nothing about it. I will tell you all the men who are
connected with the crime.

About the same time as I bought the silver set I
bought other articles, a silver ladle, enamelled, with stones from
Petroff's Yen 150.00 paid by my wife's check on the Thrift Corp.
and took delivery the next day and took it to Sarapovs. Sarapov
asked how I got so much money and I told him I got rich.

I bought a suit from Balikoff & Grigorieff for Yen 104.
I bought a fur coat and hat from Tschurin for $360.- and underwear
pyjamas, shorts from Tschurin, Eskins etc. One smoking jacket for
M.$30. from Eskins. Two dresses at $60.- for my wife from Louvre
and many other little things.

I gave my father-in-law some money, the details of
which are on a list on my desk at home. I should say Yen 300 -400.

By this time I was getting short of money and I having
acquired the taste, I wanted more of it.

Yurgens and Ushakov had left the town shortly after the
last theft from Rubanovitch's account. No Yurgens did not leave
at the same time as Ushakov. He stayed here for about a month
for I saw him on the street and told him everything was alright.
He said he was going to leave for Shanghai. I did not see him
again but got a letter from him about a month ago which was un-
signed saying that the other man could not be found in Shanghai
probably he has gone to Australia. He asked again if everything
was O.K. and I replied that it was alright.

Now when I was getting short of money, Lvoff came to my
house and asked if he could borrow money from me. I asked him
how much he wanted and he said Yen 100. We were alone in the room
at first. I told him that I didn't have any money like that, so
he said couldn't we do anything with the Bank to get money. I
said we could because previously I remembered his talking about
getting check from the check book and forging the signature.
I said we could do it because I have a check that stole from
the check book of Mrs. Popel on the day it was issued. I had
secured the check after Mr. Clark had initialled the register and
page_data.zh:
银质首饰盒。我们进去是为了给我妻子买一块手表。在买表的时候，我询问了那个盒子的价格。他说本地货币1,800元。我说太贵了，于是我们就出去了，此前已花费墨西哥银元300元为我妻子买了手表。我没有付款也没有拿走盒子，不，我记得我确实付了款，第二天我妻子来取走的。就在我们买手表的当天晚上，我告诉妻子我们可以买下那个银盒。我派了一个名叫萨拉波夫（Sarapov）的人去帮我买这个盒子，他住在亚姆斯卡亚街（Yamskaya St.），曾为我做过许多雕刻等工作。萨拉波夫与这起伪造案毫无关联。他花了1,200日元买下盒子，我让萨拉波夫替我保管。

后来我想再买点别的东西，因为我们家里从未有过什么像样的摆设。我曾向妻子解释，我的钱是通过外汇投机赚来的。

于是我们又去了库斯佩（Kuspe）那里，问他是否有银器。我们看了几套银餐具，同意以2,000日元的价格购买一套。我说我会派人去付款。我给了萨拉波夫2,000日元，他买回了那套银餐具并为我进行了雕刻。其中一半是他刻的，但他刻得很糟糕，我便让利普科夫斯基（Lipkovsky）完成剩余的雕刻工作。利普科夫斯基认识我，随后他开始谈论说我有很多钱，我解释说这是通过与日本的代理人贸易赚得的。这套银餐具上刻有我的姓名首字母缩写，一直存放在齐科夫（Zykoff）处，但昨晚我去到齐科夫那里，让他把餐具送到埃尔多拉多酒店（Hotel Eldorado），交给法沃尔斯基先生（Mr. Favorsky）。我住在那家酒店时认识了他，在我生病期间他曾照顾过我。请不要把他牵扯进来，因为他对此事一无所知。我会告诉你们所有与这起犯罪有关的人。

在我购买那套银餐具的同时，我还购买了其他物品：从彼得罗夫（Petroff）处购买了一把镶有宝石的珐琅银勺，价格为150.00日元，由我妻子开具的节俭公司（Thrift Corp.）支票支付，次日提货并送到了萨拉波夫处。萨拉波夫问我怎么会有这么多钱，我告诉他我发财了。

我从巴利科夫和格里戈里耶夫（Balikoff & Grigorieff）处花104日元买了一套西装。我从楚林（Tschurin）处花360美元买了一件皮大衣和一顶帽子，还从楚林、埃斯金斯（Eskins）等处购买了内衣、睡衣、短裤等。我从埃斯金斯处花30墨西哥银元买了一件吸烟夹克。我从卢浮宫商店（Louvre）为妻子买了两件连衣裙，每件60美元，还有许多其他小物件。

我给了岳父一些钱，具体细节列在我家中书桌上的清单上。我想大概是300至400日元。

这时我的钱开始不够用了，而且既然已经尝到了甜头，我想要更多。

尤尔根斯（Yurgens）和乌沙科夫（Ushakov）在鲁巴诺维奇（Rubanovitch）账户最后一次被盗后不久就离开了本市。不，尤尔根斯并没有和乌沙科夫同时离开。他在这里待了大约一个月，因为我在街上见过他，并告诉他一切正常。他说他打算前往上海。此后我没再见过他，但大约一个月前收到他一封未署名的信，信中说另一个人无法在上海找到，可能已经去了澳大利亚。他再次询问是否一切安好，我回复说没问题。

正当我资金短缺时，利沃夫（Lvoff，注：原文此处拼写为Lvoff，下文多为Ivoff，依上下文指同一人）来到我家，问我能否借给他钱。我问他想借多少，他说要100日元。起初房间里只有我们两人。我告诉他我没有那样的现金，于是他说我们能不能通过银行搞点钱。我说可以，因为我记得他以前曾谈论过从支票簿中取出支票并伪造签名的事。我说我们可以做，因为我有一张从波佩尔夫人（Mrs. Popel）的支票簿中偷出来的支票，那是支票开出的当天。我是在克拉克先生（Mr. Clark）在登记簿上草签并将支票簿交给勤务员送出之后拿到那张支票的。

page_data.en:
given the book to the boy to send out. I asked the boy to give me
the check book as I wanted to see if it was printed correctly.
He gave it to me and I tore out a check and then gave (the book)
it back to the boy half an hour later. That was the only check
that I ever took out of a client's book with the exception of one
for local dollars which I took out of a new book from the middle
which was lying in the right hand drawer of Mr. Clark's desk about
the same time. I think the name is Kusatkin. I destroyed this
check right after the first forgery for Yen 300.- but I kept the
check from Mrs. Popel's book. I don't think I mentioned to
Yurgens that I had this check. I took it because I thought it
might be more useful than a counter check. As I think it over
now I think the first counter check was taken several days
before the 15th of October when it was used for Yen 300.

I kept the Popel check under the Power of Attorney file
cards.

Now to return to my conversation with Ivoff.

He said it was very serious business but thought it
could be done. Then I told him that I had already done it with
counter checks and got from Okun and Rabanovitch over Yen 13,000
from the Bank. He asked me "who do you work with or do you do
it yourself". I said it was foolish to think I did it alone, but
I had men and could not tell him and would not tell him who they
were. Ivoff said if you did it it is a great idea and we can
get Yen 100,000.- from the Bank. He offered to disguise him-
self and present the checks. I told him that every dog about
Harbin knows him and that he would be recognised. But he must

get a man to get the money. He said he knew no one and I told
him to think it over. Before he went away he asked me again
for the Yen 100.- which I promised to give him that next day if
he could meet me on the corner of Pochtovaya and Novtorgovaya
Streets in Newtown.

The next day he met me the next day. This was about the
end of October and he said that he would look for a man. He knew
some people but he was afraid to tell them about it. I said it
must be a man unknown to me and one who will not betray us.

The next day he called me up on the phone and told me to
meet him at the corner of Birjevaya and Kitaiskaya Streets
between 1 and 2, at about 1.50.

I met him and we went towards the second street after
Kitaiskaya, Artilleriskaya. He told me then that a friend of his
by the name of "Mischa" (did not tell me the full name) with
whom he had talked about this business, was personally afraid to
do that, but if he (Mischa) would be paid, he would tell the
address of several people who were acquainted with this kind of
business. He said they had got money in Vladivostock by forged
checks or similar instruments. Then I told him I wanted to
have nothing to do with professionals because they would stick
to you like a leech and never let you out. He insisted on our
going to these people as he felt sure that they were reliable
people and urged me to go and meet them too - but I refused and
on that point we turned and started back to the Bank, but
before I left him, we saw Olsufieff coming behind us and I told
Ivoff that it was very awkward for us to be seen together, as
Olsufieff came up and spoke a few words, then we parted and Ivoff
went on his own and met those people whose address he had already
received from Mischa. It was at an hotel on the Birjevaya Street
and the people were one old man and one young man. He said
they were very willing but when he mentioned the amount of
U.S.$5,000.- they said it was such a trifle that they would not
bother with it.

The same day in the evening he came and told me this in
my house.
page_data.zh:
我让勤务员把支票簿给我，说我想看看印刷是否正确。他把支票簿给了我，我撕下一张支票，半小时后把（支票簿）还给了勤务员。除了另一张本地银元支票外，这是我唯一一次从客户的支票簿中取出的支票，那张本地银元支票是大约在同一时间从克拉克先生办公桌右手抽屉里放着的一本新支票簿中间取出的。我想那个名字是库萨特金（Kusatkin）。我在第一次伪造300日元支票后立刻销毁了这张支票，但我保留了从波佩尔夫人支票簿中取出的那张。我想我没有告诉尤尔根斯我有这张支票。我留下它是因为我觉得它比空白支票更有用。现在回想起来，我觉得第一张空白支票是在10月15日使用前的几天拿走的，当时用于伪造300日元。

我把波佩尔的支票藏在授权委托书档案卡片下面。

现在回到我与伊沃夫（Ivoff，即前文之Lvoff）的谈话。

他说这是一件非常严重的事情，但认为可以做。于是我告诉他，我之前已经用空白支票做过，并从奥昆（Okun）和拉巴诺维奇（Rabanovitch）那里从银行弄到了超过13,000日元。他问我：“你和谁一起干，还是你自己干？”我说认为我一个人干是很愚蠢的，但我有人手，不能告诉他，也不会告诉他他们是谁。伊沃夫说，如果你做到了，那是个好主意，我们可以从银行弄到100,000日元。他提出乔装打扮去提示支票。我告诉他，哈尔滨每条狗都认识他，他会被认出来。但他必须

找个人去取钱。他说他不认识任何人，我让他再想想。在他离开之前，他再次向我索要那100日元，我答应如果第二天他能在新城（Newtown）的波奇托瓦亚街（Pochtovaya）和诺夫托尔戈瓦亚街（Novtorgovaya）拐角处与我见面，我就给他。

第二天他见到了我。那大约是十月底，他说他会去找个人。他认识一些人，但他不敢告诉他们这件事。我说这个人必须是我完全不认识的，而且不会出卖我们。

第二天他打电话给我，让我在1点到2点之间，大约1点50分，在比尔热瓦亚街（Birjevaya）和基泰斯卡亚街（Kitaiskaya）的拐角处与他见面。

我见到他后，我们朝基泰斯卡亚街之后的第二条街——阿蒂列里斯卡亚街（Artilleriskaya）走去。他告诉我，他的一个名叫“米沙”（Mischa，未告知全名）的朋友曾与他谈论过这笔生意，此人亲自去做感到害怕，但如果付钱给米沙，米沙会提供几个熟悉此类行当的人的地址。他说这些人在符拉迪沃斯托克（Vladivostock）通过伪造支票或类似票据搞到过钱。于是我告诉他，我不想与职业罪犯有任何瓜葛，因为他们会像水蛭一样粘着你，永远甩不掉。他坚持要我们去见这些人，因为他确信他们是可靠的人，并催促我也去见见他们——但我拒绝了，在此问题上我们转身开始往回走向银行，但在我离开他之前，我们看到奥尔苏菲耶夫（Olsufieff）从后面走来，我告诉伊沃夫，被人看到我们在一起非常尴尬，因为奥尔苏菲耶夫走上前来说了几句话，然后我们分开了，伊沃夫独自去见了那些他从米沙那里得到地址的人。地点在比尔热瓦亚街的一家旅馆，那些人是一个老人和一个年轻人。他说他们很愿意干，但当他提到5,000美元的金额时，他们说这数目太小，不值得费心。

当天晚上他来到我家，告诉了我这些情况。

page_data.en:
The same afternoon I had stolen Mrs Popel's signature
card from the file. We were alone in the room and I showed him the card
He tried the signature in my room. He did not copy it through thin paper
but practised writing it on plain paper. After he practised a little he
signed Mrs. Popel's blank check in my presence in my room. Now I re-
collect these events more clearly and I remember that after the first
meeting on Birjevaya St. he called me up and said that he had been to
see these people and they were all right but said the amount was too
small but later on agreed to do it just to keep in the game. He made
an appointment for the same day and it was agreed that I should bring
the signature card to his house at Modiagow. I hired a car and went
there and left the card and told him to take good care of it. The next
day he came to my house and showed me what he could do. After practising
in my house, as I said before, I gave him the blank check and he forged
Mrs. Popel's name in my presence. Then he took the check and left and
I had previously told him how to telephone me after the check was
presented to find out if it was safe to come and get the money.

The next morning I put the card back in the file at the
Bank and at about 11 a.m. the man came. He went to Kalitz and I
noticed the check. The man was an absolute stranger to me. He
was about my size, clean shaven, with a brownish or dark overcoat
about 30/35 years old. I think I could identify him if I saw him
again. I noticed that the man was well instructed for he enquired
about the rate of exchange and disappeared. In about 10 minutes I
got a call from Ivoff and I went over to the Ivoff and saw that every
thing was ready for paying the check. I answered Ivoff that it was all
right. I did not notice how the man came and got the money. It was
agreed that between Ivoff and I that I meet him at 4 o'clock. We had
a misunderstanding as to the place and while he was awaiting me at the
corner of Post St. I was waiting near the Bank. After half an hour I
took a car to Lvoff's house in Modiago.. He was not at home so I left
a note with his brother that I would call again in the evening. Then
I rode home in the same car. I had been home about half an hour and
was just having my dinner when Ivoff came. The cook who opened the
door left him outside on the stairs and I went out to him. He talked
with me about our mistake re meeting place and he handed me some money,
which I counted in his presence. There was only Yen 4,900. It had
been agreed that I was to get as many yen as the check was in U.S.$.
The check had been in blank when signed in my house. Ivoff gave me
Yen 100 more and asked me to accept Yen 5,000 instead of Yen 5,100
plus the Yen 100 he owed me. He said he had paid Yen 3,000 to the man
who received the money at the Bank and Yen 300 to "Mischa". He told me
at that time or subsequently, I am not quite sure just when, that Mischa
had filled out the words on the check. Then he went away. He said he
would come to the Bank and he came within a few days selling health
insurance certificates. I asked him how it was with these people and
he said they had taken more money from him, Mischa got more than Yen 300
out of him.

About two weeks later there came a call for me over the
phone. It was Lvoff who told me that I must meet him urgently at
the corner of Korolkaya and Chinese Street. I came there at 1.30 p.m.
met Ivoff who said that he had an annoying letter stating that
unless Loc.$500 or Yen 500 (I do not remember which) were paid to the
bearer of a certain receipt in the office of the newspaper "Rupor",
that the affair of the forgery would be disclosed. I asked who the
man was and threatened to kill him (the man) and then myself. He said
the man was his friend Mischa, probably, because he knew the stationary
He promised to try to straighten it out and I refused to pay out any
more money.

The next day we met again and he said it was settled.
But he said that the man wanted to try and get more money from the
Bank, but I refused to help as I felt that I would be everlasting.

Ivoff said that we must do something but I refused and
said that I would get no more signature cards nor checks.

Then Ivoff said that he would help the man with information
page_data.zh:
同一天下午，我从档案中偷出了波佩尔夫人的签名卡。房间里只有我们两人，我把卡片给他看。他在我的房间里试签了名。他没有透过薄纸描摹，而是在普通纸上练习书写。练习了一会儿后，他当着我的面在我的房间里签署了波佩尔夫人的空白支票。现在我更清晰地回忆起这些事件，我记得在比尔热瓦亚街第一次会面后，他打电话给我，说他已经见过那些人，他们没问题，但说金额太小，不过后来为了继续参与此事而同意了。他约定了当天的时间，并商定我应该把签名卡带到他在莫迪亚戈（Modiagow）的家。我雇了一辆车去那里，留下了卡片，并嘱咐他好好保管。第二天他来到我家，向我展示他能做到什么程度。如前所述，在我家练习之后，我把空白支票给他，他当着我的面伪造了波佩尔夫人的签名。然后他拿着支票离开了，此前我已告诉他，在提示支票后如何通过电话联系我，以确定前来取钱是否安全。

第二天早上，我把卡片放回银行的档案中，上午11点左右那个人来了。他去找卡利茨（Kalitz），我注意到了那张支票。那个人对我来说完全是个陌生人。他身材与我相仿，面部光洁无胡须，穿着褐色或深色大衣，大约30至35岁。我想如果我再见到他，我能认出他来。我注意到这个人受过良好指导，因为他询问了汇率，随后便消失了。大约10分钟后，我接到伊沃夫的电话，我走到伊沃夫那里，看到支付支票的一切都已准备就绪。我回答伊沃夫说一切正常。我没有注意到那个人是如何来取走钱的。伊沃夫和我约定在4点钟见面。我们在见面地点上产生了误会，当他在邮局街（Post St.）拐角处等我时，我正在银行附近等待。半小时后，我乘车前往莫迪亚戈的利沃夫（Lvoff）家。他不在家，所以我给他哥哥留了张纸条，说我晚上会再来。然后我乘同一辆车回家。我到家大约半小时，正在吃晚饭时，伊沃夫来了。开门的厨师让他留在外面的楼梯上，我出去见他。他与我谈论了我们在见面地点上的失误，并递给我一些钱，我当着他的面清点了一下。只有4,900日元。此前商定的是，支票上是多少美元，我就得多少日元。支票在我家签署时是空白的。伊沃夫又给了我100日元，让我接受5,000日元，而不是5,100日元加上他欠我的100日元。他说他付给了在银行取钱的那个人3,000日元，付给“米沙”300日元。他当时或随后告诉我——我不确定确切时间——说是米沙填写了支票上的文字。然后他就走了。他说他会来银行，几天内他果然来了，推销健康保险证书。我问他那些人的情况如何，他说那些人从他那里拿了更多的钱，米沙从他那里拿走的超过了300日元。

大约两周后，我接到了一个电话。是利沃夫（Lvoff），他告诉我必须在科罗尔卡亚街（Korolkaya）和中国街（Chinese Street）的拐角处紧急与他见面。我下午1点30分到达那里，见到了伊沃夫，他说他收到一封令人烦恼的信，信中称除非向持有某张收据的人支付500本地货币或500日元（我不记得是哪种）到《鲁波尔》（Rupor）报社办公室，否则伪造案将被揭露。我问那人是谁，并威胁要杀死他（那人）然后自杀。他说那人可能是他的朋友米沙，因为米沙知道信笺纸张的情况。他答应设法解决此事，我拒绝再支付任何钱款。

第二天我们又见了面，他说事情已经解决了。但他说那人想试着从银行再搞点钱，但我拒绝帮忙，因为我觉得那样会没完没了。

伊沃夫说我们必须做点什么，但我拒绝了，并说我不会再弄任何签名卡或支票。

然后伊沃夫说他会用信息帮助那个人

page_data.en:
but nothing more. He hoped that the man would get the money and
go away from Harbin. So he said that he would send him to get a
countercheck, I told him that the man should not apply to me. He asked
whose account if Yen is the biggest so I told him Kulaeff's account
but if he tried to do anything with that he would compromise a good man
who is Kulaeff's attorney. So I suggested Naftalin, but that I would
not help at all. Then we parted, but before going Ivoff said that
it would not be necessary to give a number as he himself would put
Clark's initial over the signature.

The next day or the following day Isac came to me.
He was a little man, black hair, dark complexion, with a dark blue
overcoat whom I could probably recognise. He was very frightened.
I do not know if he came to me intentionally. He asked for a
Counter check. I asked whose name, already suspecting him from
his appearance; he said it was for "Naftalin". So I took out a
check and gave it to him. He went away. There were many people
about and I could not refuse to give it to him. One or two days later
it was quite a surprise to me to hear that forged check was caught
as I did not see the man who presented it. There was no arrangement
about calling up by telephone as I had refused to help. I did not
know how the signature was made as I merely said she signed with a L.
in front of her name. Ivoff told me that the signature would not matter
as he would keep the check from reaching Clark by forging Clark's
initial.

Afterwards Ivoff called me on the phone and arranged a
meeting. I told him the thing happened as I suspected and he must
see me as little as possible. He agreed and we parted.

I saw him once in the movies and he asked me how things
were and I said all right.

I met him again by chance and he asked me whether every
thing was alright and could we not do something else in the same
way. I said no. He told me that he had paid all his debts,
miscellaneous debts etc.

Once he called me up again on the phone and arranged a
meeting at the Prijoda Cafe. He then told me I was very careless
and showed that I had too much money. He said Lipkovsky asked him
where Chulkoff got his money. After that I told him I would settle
that and we parted.

I went to Lipkovsky and talked to him and said that I
was smuggling things into America and perhaps I would try to get
his big silver punch bowl set away. So he believed me as he was
eager to sell the bowl and he offered to sell it to me on credit.
I promised him to let him know later but told him to keep still or
rather I did not tell him to keep still - that I said now in error.

About two days ago, on Monday January the 21st Lvoff
called me again on the phone and asked to see me at Prijoda's
I met him there at 1.30 and told him that all was going fine, that
Okun's check had been found out but no one was suspected. So he
said that he was going to America in March with his wife and he did
not have enough money for both of them and he proposed to get some
drafts which could be forged and the money could be received in the
States. I said that I could not do anything with drafts but
thought that later on before he left, we could do something with
the checks. No definite plans were made then and we parted. He
said he had Yen 100 left. Before he left however that day he told
me that he had given Mischa Yen 300 more so that he could go to
Shanghai. He had already gone. He had not seen the other couple
again but said one of them had gone to Soviet Russia again via
Saghalien to get some more money. I told him that I was glad they
were away.

Now about the spending of the last Yen 5,000. By that time
the Thrift Corp. account was closed I had about Yen 5,600 after the
Popel forgery.
page_data.zh:
但没有更多了。他希望那人拿到钱后离开哈尔滨。所以他说他会派他去取一张副支票（countercheck），我告诉他那人不应该来找我。他问如果是 Yen 账户余额最大，那是谁的账户，我告诉他是 Kulaeff 的账户，但如果他试图利用那个账户做手脚，就会连累一位好人，即 Kulaeff 的律师。于是我建议用 Naftalin 的账户，但我表示完全不会提供帮助。随后我们分开了，但在离开前，Ivoff 说没必要提供号码，因为他自己会在签名上方加上 Clark 的首字母。

第二天或再过一天，Isac 来找我。他是个小个子，黑发，肤色黝黑，穿着深蓝色大衣，我应该能认出他来。他非常惊恐。我不知道他是否是故意来找我的。他索要一张副支票。我问是谁的名字，从他的外表我已经对他产生了怀疑；他说是要给“Naftalin”的。于是我拿出一张支票交给他。他走了。周围有很多人，我无法拒绝给他。一两天后，听说那张伪造支票被查获，这让我十分惊讶，因为我并没有见到递交支票的人。既然我已拒绝帮忙，也就没有关于通过电话联系的安排。我不知道签名是如何伪造的，因为我只是说她在名字前面签了一个 L。Ivoff 告诉我签名无关紧要，因为他会通过伪造 Clark 的首字母来阻止支票到达 Clark 手中。

后来 Ivoff 打电话给我，约定见面。我告诉他事情正如我所怀疑的那样发生了，他必须尽量少见我。他同意了，我们便分开了。

我在电影院见过他一次，他问我情况如何，我说一切正常。

我又偶然遇见了他，他问是否一切都好，我们能否以同样的方式再做点什么。我说不行。他告诉我他已经还清了所有债务，包括杂项债务等。

有一次他又打电话给我，约定在 Prijoda 咖啡馆见面。他当时说我太粗心大意，并指出我持有的现金过多。他说 Lipkovsky 问他 Chulkoff 的钱是从哪里来的。之后我告诉他我会处理这件事，我们便分开了。

我去找了 Lipkovsky 并与他交谈，说我在向美国走私物品，也许我会试着把他那套大型银质 punch bowl（潘趣酒碗）弄走。于是他相信了我，因为他急于出售这套酒碗，并提出赊账卖给我。我答应他稍后通知他，但让他保持沉默——或者更确切地说，我并没有让他保持沉默，这是我现在的错误说法。

大约两天前，即 1 月 21 日星期一，Lvoff 又打电话给我，要求在 Prijoda 咖啡馆见我。我于下午 1:30 在那里与他见面，并告诉他一切进展顺利，Okun 的支票已被发现是伪造的，但没有人受到怀疑。于是他说他将于三月与妻子前往美国，两人的资金不足，他提议搞一些可以伪造的汇票，以便在美国取款。我说我对汇票无能为力，但认为在他离开之前，我们或许可以在支票上做点文章。当时没有制定具体计划，我们便分开了。他说他还剩 100 日元。不过在那天离开前，他告诉我他又给了 Mischa 300 日元，以便他能去上海。Mischa 已经走了。他没有再见到另一对夫妇，但说其中一人已再次经萨哈林岛（Saghalien）前往苏俄获取更多资金。我告诉他我很高兴他们已经离开。

现在谈谈最后 5,000 日元的开销。那时 Thrift Corp. 的账户已关闭，在 Popel 伪造案之后，我手头约有 5,600 日元。

page_data.en:
I went to Zykoff and asked him to take the money. I refused
to tell him from where I got it, but he finally accepted. I told
him to open an account which he did. I can definitely state how it
was used by referring to the ledger in the Bank. Roughly I would
say as follows:

Yen 850 for a second silver box (Loc. 120, exact cost)
from Krape's.

Zykoff bought this for me and took it home with other box
from Sarapov's. I sent the silver valuables on to Zykoff.

I used Loc. 154S to pay a debt of my father-in-law which
was at the Bank of the Landowners. The money was paid to Lin Tui
by myself personally in the presence of my father-in-law.

I refused to tell my father-in-law from where I got the
money but said it was honestly made.

Yen 520 for a ring for my wife.

Loc. 150.- )
& Yen 100.- ) to my mother-in-law.

The $150 was given on account of a brooch with an amethyst
stone which my mother-in-law gave to my wife.

Yen 100) Given to my father-in-law.
Loc. 3 40)
Loc. 3 90) For lodging.
and other amounts from time to time. I have a full record at home
and believe the amount to be about Yen 2000. from the very
beginning - that is including Loc. 420 in January 1928.

Loc. 162 paid to Tschurins for my account.

Many small amounts for my family - Petroff's, Grocery bills,
etc.

Loc. } Six hundred on vexils for $200 and $200 to Mendrin,
which my father-in-law arranged. I gave him the money and he got
the vexils. Of this amount $400 has been paid on account and
the balance of $600.00 is promised for payment this week.

Loc. $275.00 I loaned to my friend, Dr. Roversky - who
promised to pay it back by the beginning of February.

Loc. 100 to Sarapov for engraving and I also loaned him
Loc. $50.00.

I also bought many sundry things for my wife and for myself,
and little present for my father and mother-in-law - cane and bag.

I deposited U.S. $430 to an account in the name of my wife.

Loc. 360 I gave to Zykoff and other small amounts.

All the above mentioned loans and valuables, deposits, etc.
I hereby authorize the Bank to receive as a partial payment of the
money which I took from the Bank.

Finally I wish to state that I alone am guilty with the people
whom I have definitely specified in this statement. I am ready to
swear to the truth of this statement in Court and ready to bear any
punishment, but as a favour I ask for all those innocent parties to
go unmolested.

I have no money now except $4 in cash.
page_data.zh:
我去找 Zykoff，让他收下这笔钱。我拒绝告诉他钱的来源，但他最终接受了。我让他开立一个账户，他照办了。通过查阅银行账簿，我可以明确说明这笔钱是如何使用的。大致情况如下：

850 日元用于购买第二个银盒（地点编号 120，确切成本），购自 Krape 店。

Zykoff 为我购买了此物，并将其与从 Sarapov 店购买的其他盒子一起带回家。我将银器贵重物品寄给了 Zykoff。

我使用地点编号 154S 支付了我岳父在地主银行（Bank of the Landowners）的一笔债务。这笔钱是我在我岳父在场的情况下亲自支付给 Lin Tui 的。

我拒绝告诉岳父钱的来源，但说是正当所得。

520 日元用于给我妻子买一枚戒指。

地点编号 150.- )
及 100 日元.- ) 给我岳母。

这 150 美元是作为一枚紫水晶胸针的部分款项支付的，该胸针是我岳母送给我妻子的。

100 日元) 给我岳父。
地点编号 3 40)
地点编号 3 90) 用于住宿。
以及其他不时发生的金额。我家里有一份完整记录，相信从最初开始——即包括 1928 年 1 月的地点编号 420——总额约为 2,000 日元。

地点编号 162 支付给 Tschurins，记在我的账上。

许多用于家庭的小额开支——Petroff 店、杂货账单等。

地点编号 } 六百用于购买 vexils（原文不清，可能指证券或某种票据），价值 200 美元，另付 200 美元给 Mendrin，这是我岳父安排的。我把钱给了他，他买回了 vexils。这笔款项中已有 400 美元作为预付款支付，剩余 600.00 美元承诺本周支付。

地点编号 275.00 美元借给我的朋友 Roversky 博士——他承诺在二月初归还。

地点编号 100 给 Sarapov 用于雕刻费用，我还借给他地点编号 50.00 美元。

我还为我和妻子购买了许多杂物，并为我的父母和岳父母买了一些小礼物——手杖和包。

我以我妻子的名义存入 430 美元到一个账户中。

地点编号 360 我给 Zykoff 及其他小额款项。

上述所有贷款、贵重物品、存款等，我在此授权银行接收，作为我从银行取走款项的部分偿还。

最后我想声明，只有我与本陈述中明确指定的人有罪。我准备在法庭上宣誓本陈述属实，并愿意接受任何惩罚，但作为一种恩惠，我请求让所有无辜者不受打扰。

我现在除了 4 美元现金外，身无分文。

page_data.en:
Signed in the presence of J.L. Hutcheson and J.L. Curtis
in whose presence this statement was made.

All the sheets of this report, thirty-six sheets are signed
by me after having read them over.

(sgd) Alex. Malakoff.
page_data.zh:
在 J.L. Hutcheson 和 J.L. Curtis 面前签署，本陈述是在他们面前作出的。

本报告的所有页张，共三十六页，在我阅读后均由我签名。

(签名) Alex. Malakoff.

February 7, 1929.

The C.I.D.,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
Shanghai.

Dear Sir,

With reference to the case of the National City Bank
against Yergens and others we beg to enclose for your in-
formation copy of the confession of Chulkoff. As we have
received only one copy, will you please return this copy to
us so that we can have parts of it translated. We should
like to get this copy back as soon as possible for this
purpose.

We have suggested to the National City Bank in Harbin
that they request the police there to send you a certified
copy of this confession so as to have it come through official
channels.

In the event that you should have already received a copy
of this confession and have translated it will you please let
us know as this would save a great deal of time.

Yours very truly,

FLEMING, FRANKLIN & ALTMAN.

Enclosure.

NFA/NR.

敬启者：

关于花旗银行起诉 Yergens 等人一案，谨随函附上 Chulkoff 供词副本一份，供贵方参考。由于我们只收到一份副本，请将该副本退还给我们，以便我们翻译部分内容。为此目的，我们希望尽快收回该副本。

page_data.en:
COPY
Harbin, Manchuria,
January 23rd, 1929.

CONFESSION OF CHULKOFF.

THE START:
I was talking with Ivoff who spoke of how easy it is to get money from the Bank from forged checks. We discussed how easy it would be to copy the signatures say on a check from a book just issued. He said that if a check from a customer's check book could be obtained and the signature forged it would go through easily and the Bank would not accept responsibility. Even a counter check if the signature was correct could be safely cashed providing the forgery was good enough. At that time nothing more was said. That was about in July or August.

We discussed the possibility of securing money in this way but arranged nothing definite up to the time Ivoff left. We thought that as Clark was new and inexperienced, with too much work to check up things carefully that such a plan would succeed. Young was much more careless; he would sign anything without any particular attention. But he was only there for 1½ months after I joined the Bank and before we discussed this way of getting money.

I kept thinking about what Ivoff and I had talked and felt tempted to get some money as it was urgently needed at home, where my father-in-law sold everything to pay back the money he took (about Loc. $5,000.-).

A man came from Shanghai by the name of Vladimir Nicholaevitch Yurgens about September. His address is Ave. Joffre No. 536, Apartment 6, Shanghai where he is probably now. I knew him in Vladivostock in 1922 - or rather 1923 and became quite good friends with him.

I met Yurgens on the street and went with him to a cafe but did not take him home.

He told me that he was desperately in need of money and would do anything to get that money. I told him I was working in a Bank.

A few days later, by appointment we met again and he told me about instances of getting money from Banks and he had been in our Bank and saw our system. He suggested that we could get some money out of the Bank, a few thousand (he needed about Yen 10,000) and I had been thinking it over and decided that we might try. I didn't want to try too large a sum as I thought we would be caught and I didn't wish to take any risk. I agreed and explained how it could be done.

Anyone could apply for and receive a counter check. Then I could get the signature card, we could fill the check on an account, whose balance was known. He agreed to do the forgery and fill in the check but he said that he couldn't come to get the money personally as he was known in the city and might be recognised. He said, however, that he would send a man and I asked who. He said his name was Ushakov, who lived on Commercial Street. He said the man would leave the town afterwards so that he would not betray us. We discussed who it could be and picked out two rich Jews - Okun and Rubanovitch.

We found that Okun had Yen 3,000.- in his account and Rubanovitch about US$1,000. So we decided to start with Yen 300. Yurgens came and got a counter check from Hults. The same day I took out the signature card after 1 p.m. and gave it to Yurgens that afternoon. Next morning at 8.05 in Newtown he met me by appointment and gave back the signature card and showed me the check the forged signature looked very good to me and we arranged that
page_data.zh:
副本
满洲，哈尔滨，
1929年1月23日。

丘尔科夫的供词。

起因：
我与伊沃夫（Ivoff）交谈，他谈到通过伪造支票从银行获取钱财是多么容易。我们讨论了复制刚发出的支票簿上签名的简便性。他说，如果能弄到客户支票簿中的一张支票并伪造签名，就能顺利兑现，银行也不会承担责任。即使是柜台支票，只要签名逼真，伪造得足够好，也能安全兑现。当时没有再谈更多。那大约是在七月或八月。

我们讨论了以这种方式获取钱财的可能性，但在伊沃夫离开之前并未做出任何具体安排。我们认为，由于克拉克（Clark）是新来的，缺乏经验，且工作繁忙无暇仔细核查，这样的计划会成功。扬（Young）则粗心得多；他会不加特别注意地签署任何文件。但他在我进入银行后仅待了一个半月，在我们讨论这种搞钱方法之前他就离开了。

我一直在思考我和伊沃夫的谈话，并感到诱惑想去弄点钱，因为家里急需用钱，我的岳父变卖了一切来偿还他拿走的钱（约规元5,000元）。

大约在九月，一个叫弗拉基米尔·尼古拉耶维奇·于尔根斯（Vladimir Nicholaevitch Yurgens）的人从上海来到哈尔滨。他的地址是上海霞飞路536号6室，他现在可能还住在那里。我于1922年——或者更确切地说是1923年——在符拉迪沃斯托克认识了他，并与他成为了相当好的朋友。

我在街上遇到于尔根斯，和他一起去了一家咖啡馆，但没有带他回家。

他告诉我他极度缺钱，为了搞到钱愿意做任何事。我告诉他我在一家银行工作。

几天后，我们按约定再次见面，他向我讲述了从银行搞钱的案例，说他曾去过我们要行并了解了我们的制度。他建议我们可以从银行弄出一些钱，几千块（他需要约日元10,000元），我经过考虑，决定我们可以试一试。我不想尝试太大的金额，因为我认为我们会被抓，我也不想承担任何风险。我同意了，并解释了如何操作。

任何人都可以申请并领取一张柜台支票。然后我可以取出签名卡，我们在一个余额已知的账户上填写支票。他同意进行伪造并填写支票，但他说他不能亲自来取钱，因为他在城里有人认识，可能会被认出来。不过他说，他会派一个人来，我问是谁。他说那人叫乌沙科夫（Ushakov），住在商业街（Commercial Street）。他说事后这个人会离开这座城市，这样就不会出卖我们。我们讨论了目标人选，挑中了两个富有的犹太人——奥昆（Okun）和鲁巴诺维奇（Rubanovitch）。

我们发现奥昆的账户里有日元3,000元，鲁巴诺维奇约有美元1,000元。所以我们决定先从日元300元开始。于尔根斯来并从赫尔茨（Hults）那里拿到了一张柜台支票。同一天下午1点后，我取出了签名卡，并在当天下午交给了于尔根斯。第二天早上8点05分，他在新城（Newtown）按约定与我见面，归还了签名卡，并给我看了那张支票，伪造的签名在我看来非常逼真，我们商定

page_data.en:
his man should come to the Bank and I would give him a brass
check for the forged check and then he should go out of the Bank.
In case the check was found forged I was to notify Yurgens when
he called me up on the phone. I was so disturbed, that I even
forgot to have Ushakov endorse the check. Yurgens called me up
in 15 minutes and I replied that "my health was good" which meant
that the check is O.K. and he must send Ushakov in to get the
money. He came and got it but I did not watch for him nor see
him.

We were elated over this and decided to try again.
I remember watching Clark when he compared the first signature
and he hesitated a little but passed it.

This time I had received Yen 100.- Yurgens took Yen
200.- to divide with Ushakov.

On the 16th October we had another meeting and as
everything had gone well we decided to do it again for a bigger
amount. So on the 17th Yurgens got another counter check and I
gave him the signature card again in the afternoon. The next
morning he showed me the forged check, which I found O.K. and I
replaced the signature card when Clark was busy at the counter.
Ushakov came again and we followed the same procedure, obtaining
Yen 2,700.- of which Ushakov, as Yurgens said, had received Yen
700. He kept Yen 1,000 for himself and gave me Yen 1,000.

I had already used up the Yen 100.- in paying bills
at Petroff's, a grocery store, armies etc. With the Yen 1,000.-
which I had in my pocket, I bought in a few days a $30.- tea
spoon, fork and tongs at Itzikson's and deposited Yen 300.- back
to Okun's account, with no good reason for doing so except that
I had too much money. I gave my wife Yen 800.- and told her to
deposit the money to her account in the Thrift Corporation. She
asked where the money came from as we had never had any before
and wanted to open a joint account and I told her that I made the
money by speculating on currencies. She believed me and took the
money there. I made a mistake in saying that I deposited Yen 300.-
out of the cash in my pocket to Okun's account. That came later.

Yurgens came again and said that we must do it again.
I refused to join him and said if he wanted to he could do it on
his own account. We quarrelled. He came again and said that
if I refused to do it he would write a letter to certain people
and would clear out of town himself. Thereupon I agreed to do it
again. He told me to find out the balance of Rabinovitch, which
I got from the weekly balance book. Yurgens said he would not
come to the Bank himself, but told me to get two counter checks
in U.S.$, which I did on the following day. I gave them to him
with the signature card, which he returned to me on the following
morning and showed me two checks not yet filled in except for
the forged signatures. I said I didn't like one and wanted to
destroy it but he wouldn't give it to me. I told him to put
U.S.$3,000.- on one which was to be the last one.

The same day Ushakov came to the Bank and presented
two checks, one for U.S.$3,100.- and one for U.S.$3,800.- to me.
I asked Tsizik to give him numbers for the checks which he did.
I calculated the amount of Yen and asked Kailitz to write out
the contract. I laid the check and contract on Clark's desk.
Clark examined the signatures on both checks and then personally
looked at the balance in the ledger. Then he initialled them
and they went through. Yurgens telephoned again and I gave the
usual reply. Ushakov came and got the money.

We met, Yurgens and I, after 1 p.m. and I got Yen 5,000
On the same day I deposited Yen 300.- to Okun's account so as to
make the check for Yen 300.- look correct. Within a few days say
about a week my wife and I were walking by Kaspe's and saw the sign
page_data.zh:
他的人应该来银行，我会给他一个铜牌作为交换伪造支票的凭证，然后他离开银行。
如果支票被发现是伪造的，我在于尔根斯打电话给我时通知他。我当时非常紧张，甚至
忘了让乌沙科夫在支票背面背书。于尔根斯在15分钟后给我打了电话，我回答说“我身体很好”，这意味
着支票没问题，他必须派乌沙科夫进去取钱。乌沙科夫来了并取走了钱，但我没有盯着他，也没看见他。

我们为此感到兴奋，并决定再试一次。
我记得观察克拉克核对第一个签名时，他犹豫了一下，但还是通过了。

这次我得到了日元100元。于尔根斯拿了日元
200元去与乌沙科夫分赃。

10月16日，我们又见了一次面，鉴于一切顺利，我们决定再次作案，但金额更大。因此，17日于尔根斯又拿到了一张柜台支票，我在下午再次将签名卡交给了他。第二天早上，他给我看了伪造的支票，我觉得没问题，趁克拉克在柜台忙碌时，我将签名卡放回原处。乌沙科夫又来了，我们遵循同样的程序，获得了日元2,700元，其中据于尔根斯说，乌沙科夫分得了日元700元。于尔根斯自己留下了日元1,000元，给了我日元1,000元。

我已经把之前的日元100元花在彼得罗夫（Petroff）杂货店付账单、军饷等开销上了。用口袋里的这日元1,000元，我在几天内从伊齐克森（Itzikson）店里买了一套价值30美元的茶匙、叉子和火钳，并将日元300元存回奥昆的账户，这样做除了因为我钱太多之外没有别的正当理由。我给了妻子日元800元，让她把钱存入节俭公司（Thrift Corporation）她的账户里。她问钱是从哪里来的，因为我们以前从未有过这么多钱，她想开一个联名账户，我告诉她我是通过外汇投机赚的钱。她相信了我，把钱存了进去。我说我用口袋里的现金向奥昆账户存入日元300元是个错误。那是后来发生的事。

于尔根斯又来了，说我们必须再干一次。
我拒绝参与，并说如果他想干，可以单干。我们吵了一架。他又来了，说
如果我拒绝，他就会给某些人写信，并自己逃离这座城市。于是我又同意再干一次。他让我查明拉比诺维奇（Rabinovitch）的余额，我从每周余额簿中查到了。于尔根斯说他不会亲自来银行，而是让我弄两张美元柜台支票，我在第二天照办了。我把支票连同签名卡交给他，他在第二天早上还给了我，并给我看了两张除了伪造签名外尚未填写的支票。我说我不喜欢其中一张，想销毁它，但他不肯给我。我让他在那张将是最后一张的支票上填上美元3,000元。

同一天，乌沙科夫来到银行，向我出示了两张支票，一张金额为美元3,100元，另一张为美元3,800元。我请齐齐克（Tsizik）给他支票编号，他照做了。我计算了日元金额，并请凯利茨（Kailitz）写出单据。我把支票和单据放在克拉克的桌上。克拉克检查了两张支票上的签名，然后亲自查看了分类账中的余额。随后他在上面签了字，支票便顺利兑现。于尔根斯又打来电话，我给出了惯常的回答。乌沙科夫来取走了钱。

下午1点后，我和于尔根斯见了面，我分得日元5,000元。
同一天，我向奥昆的账户存入了日元300元，以便使那张日元300元的支票看起来账目正确。大约一周后的几天里，我和妻子路过卡斯佩（Kaspe）的店，看到了招牌

page_data.en:
silver jewel box. We had gone inside to buy a watch for my
wife. While buying the watch I enquired the price of the box.
He said Loc. Jl,300. I said it was too much and we went out,
after having bought a watch for my wife for Mex $300. I did not
pay for it or take it, no, I remember I did pay for it and the next
day my wife came to take it. On the same evening when we bought the
watch, I told my wife we could buy the silver box. I sent a man
named Sarapov, who lives on Yamskaya St., and who has done many
things for me, engravings etc. to buy the box for me. Sarapov is
in no way connected with this forgery business. He bought it for
Yen 1,200.- and I asked Sarapov to keep it for me.

Then I wanted to buy something else as we never had
anything pretty in our house. I had explained to my wife that I
got the money by speculations on currencies.

So we went again to Kaspe's and asked if he had
silverware. We looked at the silver sets and agreed to buy one
for Yen 2,000. I said I would send my man who would pay for it.
I gave Sarapov Yen 2,000 and he got the silver set which he en-
graved for me. One half of it he engraved for me, but he did it
so badly, I had Lipkovsky do the balance of engraving. Lipkovsky
knows me and then he started talking that I had a lot of money and
I explained that. I did it by trading with agents in Japan. The
silver set is engraved with my own initials and was kept at Zykoffs,
but last night I went to Zykoff's and asked him to take it to the
Hotel Eldorado, and leave them with Mr. Favorsky, who I came to
know when I was living at that hotel and he took care of me when
I was ill. Please do not mix him up with this as he knows abso-
lutely nothing about it. I will tell you all the men who are
connected with the crime.

About the same time as I bought the silver set I
bought other articles, a silver ladle, enamelled, with stones from
Petroff's Yen 150.00 paid by my wife's check on the Thrift Corp.
and took delivery the next day and took it to Sarapovs. Sarapov
asked how I got so much money and I told him I got rich.

I bought a suit from Balikoff & Grigorieff for Yen 104.
I bought a fur coat and hat from Tschurin for $360.- and underwear
pyjamas, shorts from Tschurin, Eskins etc. One smoking jacket for
$80. from Eskins. Two dresses at $60.- for my wife from Louvre
and many other little things.

I gave my father-in-law some money, the details of
which are on a list on my desk at home. I should say Yen 300 -400.

By this time I was getting short of money and I having
acquired the taste, I wanted more of it.

Yurgens and Ushakov had left the town shortly after the
last theft from Rubanovitch's account. No Yurgens did not leave
at the same time as Ushakov. He stayed here for about a month
for I saw him on the street and told him everything was alright.
He said he was going to leave for Shanghai. I did not see him
again but got a letter from him about a month ago which was un-
signed saying that the other man could not be found in Shanghai
probably he has gone to Australia. He asked again if everything
was O.K. and I replied that it was alright.

Now when I was getting short of money, Lvoff came to my
house and asked if he could borrow money from me. I asked him
how much he wanted and he said Yen 100. We were alone in the room
at first. I told him that I didn't have any money like that, so
he said couldn't we do anything with the Bank to get money. I
said we could because previously I remembered his talking about
getting check from the check book and forging the signature.
I said we could do it because I have a check that stole from
the check book of Mrs. Popel on the day it was issued. I had
secured the check after Mr. Clark had initialled the register and
page_data.zh:
银首饰盒。我们走进去想给我妻子买一块手表。买手表时，我询问了盒子的价格。
他说要规元1,300元。我说太贵了，我们就出来了，之后给我妻子买了一块价值墨西哥银元300元的手表。我没有付款也没有拿走，不，我记得我确实付了款，第二天我妻子来取货。就在我们买手表的当晚，我告诉妻子我们可以买那个银盒子。我派了一个名叫萨拉波夫（Sarapov）的人去帮我买盒子，他住在亚姆斯卡亚街（Yamskaya St.），曾为我做过许多事情，如雕刻等。萨拉波夫与这起伪造案毫无关联。他花了日元1,200元买下盒子，我让萨拉波夫替我保管。

然后我想买点别的东西，因为我们家里从来没有漂亮的东西。我已向妻子解释过，钱是我通过外汇投机赚来的。

所以我们又去了卡斯佩的店，问他是否有银器。我们看了银餐具套装，同意以日元2,000元购买一套。我说我会派我的人来付款。我给了萨拉波夫日元2,000元，他买下了银餐具套装并为我进行了雕刻。其中一半是他刻的，但他刻得很糟糕，我让利普科夫斯基（Lipkovsky）完成了剩下的雕刻工作。利普科夫斯基认识我，于是他开始议论我有很多钱，我便向他做了解释。我说我是通过与日本的代理商贸易赚的钱。银餐具上刻有我的姓名首字母缩写，存放在齐科夫（Zykoffs）那里，但昨晚我去齐科夫那里，请他把餐具送到埃尔多拉多酒店（Hotel Eldorado），交给法沃尔斯基先生（Mr. Favorsky），我住在那家酒店时认识了他，我生病时他曾照顾过我。请不要把他牵扯进来，因为他对此事一无所知。我会告诉你所有与这起犯罪有关的人。

大约在买银餐具的同时，我还买了其他物品，从彼得罗夫（Petroff）那里买了一把镶石头的珐琅银勺，价款日元150.00元，由我妻子开具的节俭公司支票支付，第二天提货并送到了萨拉波夫处。萨拉波夫问我怎么有这么多钱，我告诉他我发财了。

我从巴利科夫和格里戈里耶夫（Balikoff & Grigorieff）那里买了一套西装，花费日元104元。我从楚林（Tschurin）那里买了一件皮大衣和一顶帽子，花费360美元，还从楚林、埃斯金斯（Eskins）等处买了内衣、睡衣、短裤。从埃斯金斯那里买了一件吸烟夹克，花费80美元。从卢浮宫（Louvre）为我妻子买了两件连衣裙，每件60美元，还有许多其他小物件。

我给了岳父一些钱，详细清单在我家里的书桌上。大概是日元300-400元。

这时我开始手头拮据，既然已经尝到了甜头，我想要更多的钱。

于尔根斯和乌沙科夫在最后一次从鲁巴诺维奇账户盗窃后不久就离开了这座城市。不，于尔根斯并没有和乌沙科夫同时离开。他在这里待了大约一个月，因为我在街上见过他，并告诉他一切正常。他说他打算去上海。我再也没见过他，但大约一个月前收到他一封未署名的信，说另一个人（指乌沙科夫）在上海找不到，可能去了澳大利亚。他再次询问是否一切正常，我回复说没事。

现在当我手头缺钱时，利沃夫（Lvoff）来到我家，问我能否借给他钱。我问他要多少，他说要日元100元。起初房间里只有我们两人。我告诉他我没有那样的钱，于是他说我们能不能利用银行搞点钱。我说可以，因为我记得他之前谈过从支票本里拿支票并伪造签名的事。我说我们可以做，因为我有一张从波佩尔夫人（Mrs. Popel）的支票本里偷来的支票，是在签发当天偷的。我是在克拉克先生在登记簿上签字确认后拿到这张支票的

page_data.en:
given the book to the boy to send out. I asked the boy to give me
the check book as I wanted to see if it was printed correctly.
He gave it to me and I tore out a check and then gave (the book)
it back to the boy half an hour later. That was the only check
that I ever took out of a client's book with the exception of one
for local dollars which I took out of a new book from the middle
which was lying in the right hand drawer of Mr. Clark's desk about
the same time. I think the name is Kasatkin. I destroyed this
check right after the first forgery for Yen 300.- but I kept the
check from Mrs. Popel's book. I don't think I mentioned to
Jurgens that I had this check. I took it because I thought it
might be more useful than a counter check. As I think it over
now I think the first counter check was taken several days
before the 15th of October when it was used for Yen 300.

I kept the Popel check under the Power of Attorney file
cards.

Now to return to my conversation with Ivoff.

He said it was very serious business but thought it
could be done. Then I told him that I had already done it with
counter checks and got from Okun and Rubanovitch over Yen 13,000
from the Bank. He asked me "who do you work with or do you do
it yourself". I said it was foolish to think I did it alone, but
I had men and could not tell him and would not tell him who they
were. Ivoff said if you did it it is a great idea and we can
get Yen 100,000.- from the Bank. He offered to disguise him-
self and present the checks. I told him that every dog about
Harbin knows him and that he would be recognised. But he must

get a man to get the money. He said he knew no one and I told
him to think it over. Before he went away he asked me again
for the Yen 100.- which I promised to give him the next day if
he could meet me on the corner of Pochtovaya and Novtorsovaya
Streets in Newtown.

The next day he met me the next day. This was about the
end of October and he said that he would look for a man. He knew
some people but he was afraid to tell them about it. I said it
must be a man unknown to me and one who will not betray us.

The next day he called me up on the phone and told me to
meet him at the corner of Birjevaya and Kitaiskaya Streets
between 1 and 2, at about 1.50.

I met him and we went towards the second street after
Kitaiskaya, Artilleriskaya. He told me then that a friend of his
by the name of "Mischa" (did not tell me the full name) with
whom he had talked about this business, was personally afraid to
do that, but if he (Mischa) would be paid, he would tell the
address of several people who were acquainted with this kind of
business. He said they had got money in Vladivostock by forged
checks or similar instruments. Then I told him I wanted to
have nothing to do with professionals because they would stick
to you like a leech and never let you out. He insisted on our
going to these people as he felt sure that they were reliable
people and urged me to go and meet them too - but I refused and
on that point we turned and started back to the Bank, but
before I left him, we saw Olsufieff coming behind us and I told
Ivoff that it was very awkward for us to be seen together, as
Olsufieff came up and spoke a few words, then we parted and Ivoff
went on his own and met those people whose address he had already
received from Mischa. It was at an hotel on the Birjevaya Street
and the people were one old man and one young man. He said
they were very willing but when he mentioned the amount of
U.S.$5,000.- they said it was such a trifle that they would not
bother with it.

The same day in the evening he came and told me this in
my house.
page_data.zh:
把书交给那个男孩让他送出去。我要了那本支票簿，想看看印刷是否正确。他把它给了我，我撕下一张支票，半小时后把（那本）书还给了男孩。除了另一张从克拉克先生（Mr. Clark）办公桌右手抽屉里放着的一本新支票簿中间取出的一张本地银元支票外，这是我唯一一次从客户的支票簿中取出的支票。我想那个名字是卡萨特金（Kasatkin）。我在第一次伪造300日元支票后立刻销毁了这张支票，但我保留了波佩尔夫人（Mrs. Popel）支票簿中的那张支票。我想我没有告诉尤尔根斯（Jurgens）我持有这张支票。我留下它是因为我觉得它可能比柜台支票更有用。现在回想起来，我认为第一张柜台支票是在10月15日使用于300日元之前的几天取出的。

我把波佩尔的支票放在授权委托书档案卡片下面。

现在回到我与伊沃夫（Ivoff）的谈话。

他说这是一件非常严重的事情，但认为可以做成。然后我告诉他，我已经用柜台支票做过了，并从奥昆（Okun）和鲁巴诺维奇（Rubanovitch）那里从银行弄到了13,000多日元。他问我：“你和谁一起干，还是你自己干？”我说认为我一个人干是愚蠢的，但我有人手，不能告诉他，也不会告诉他他们是谁。伊沃夫说，如果你做了，那是个好主意，我们可以从银行弄到100,000日元。他提出乔装打扮去提示支票。我告诉他，哈尔滨每只狗都认识他，他会被认出来。但他必须

找个人去取钱。他说他不认识任何人，我让他再想想。在他离开之前，他又向我要那100日元，我答应如果第二天他能在新城（Newtown）的波奇托瓦亚街（Pochtovaya）和诺夫托尔索瓦亚街（Novtorsovaya）的拐角处与我见面，我就给他。

第二天他见了我。这大约是十月底，他说他会找个人。他认识一些人，但他不敢告诉他们这件事。我说这个人必须是我不知道的，而且不会出卖我们的人。

第二天他打电话给我，让我在1点到2点之间，大约1点50分，在比尔热瓦亚街（Birjevaya）和基泰斯卡亚街（Kitaiskaya）的拐角处见他。

我见到了他，我们朝基泰斯卡亚街之后的第二条街，即阿蒂列里斯卡亚街（Artilleriskaya）走去。他当时告诉我，他的一个名叫“米沙”（Mischa）（没告诉我全名）的朋友，他曾与此人谈过这笔生意，此人亲自害怕做这件事，但如果给他报酬，他（米沙）会提供几个熟悉这类生意的人的地址。他说他们在符拉迪沃斯托克（Vladivostock）通过伪造支票或类似票据搞到了钱。然后我告诉他，我不想与职业罪犯有任何瓜葛，因为他们会像水蛭一样粘着你，永远不放手。他坚持要我们去见这些人，因为他确信他们是可靠的人，并催促我也去见他们——但我拒绝了，在那一点上我们转身开始返回银行，但在我离开他之前，我们看到奥尔苏菲耶夫（Olsufieff）从后面走来，我告诉伊沃夫，被人看到我们在一起非常尴尬，因为奥尔苏菲耶夫走上前来说了几句话，然后我们分开了，伊沃夫独自去见了那些他从米沙那里已经得到地址的人。地点在比尔热瓦亚街的一家旅馆，那些人是一个老人和一个年轻人。他说他们很愿意干，但当他提到5,000美元的金额时，他们说这太微不足道了，不值得费心。

同一天晚上，他来到我家告诉我这件事。

page_data.en:
The same afternoon I had stolen Mrs Popel's signature
card from the file. We were alone in the room and I showed him the card
I'd tried the signature in my room. He did not copy it through thin paper
but practised writing it on plain paper. After he practised a little he
signed Mrs. Popel's blank check in my presence in my room. Now I re-
collect these events more clearly and I remember that after the first
meeting on Birjevaya St. he called me up and said that he had been to
see these people and they were all right but said the amount was too
small but later on agreed to do it just to keep in the gang. He made
an appointment for the same day and it was agreed that I should bring
the signature card to his house at Kodiagov. I hired a car and went
there and left the card and told him to take good care of it. The next
day he came to my house and showed me what he could do. After practising
in my house, as I said before, I gave him the blank check and he forged
Mrs. Popel's name in my presence. Then he took the check and left and
I had previously told him how to telephone me after the check was
presented to find out if it was safe to come and get the money.

The next morning I put the card back in the file at the
bank and at about 11 a.m. the man came. He went to Liltz and I
noticed the check. The man was an absolute stranger to me. He
was about my size, clean shaven, with a brownish or dark overcoat
about 30/35 years old. I think I could identify him if I saw him
again. I noticed that the man was well instructed for he enquired
about the rate of exchange and disappeared. In about 15 minutes I
got a call from Ivoff and I went over to the office and saw that every-
thing was ready for cashing the check. I answered Ivoff that it was all
right. I did not advise nor the man come and got the money. It was
agreed that between Ivoff and I that I meet him at 4 o'clock. We had
a misunderstanding as to the place and while he was waiting me at the
corner of Post St. I was waiting near the bank. After half an hour I
took a car to Lvoff's home in Kodiagov. He was not at home so I left
a note with his brother that I would call again in the evening. Then
I rode home in the same car. I had been home about half an hour and
was just having my dinner when Ivoff came. The cook who opened the
door left him outside on the stairs and I went out to him. He talked
with me about our mistake regarding place and he handed me some money,
which I counted in his presence. There was only Yen 4,900. It had
been agreed that I was to get as many yen as the check was in U.S.$.
The check had been in blank when signed in my house. Lvoff gave me
Yen 100 more and asked me to accept Yen 5,000 instead of Yen 5,100
plus the Yen 100 he owed me. He said he had paid Yen 3,000 to the man
who received the money at the bank and Yen 200 to "Mischa". He told me
at that time or subsequently, I am not quite sure just when, that Mischa
had filled out the words on the check. Then he went away. He said he
would come to the bank and he came within a few days selling health
insurance certificates. I asked him how it was with these people and
he said they had taken more money from him, Mischa got more than Yen 300
out of him.

About two weeks later there came a call for me over the
phone. It was Lvoff who told me that I must meet him urgently at
the corner of Korolkuya and Chinese Street. I came there at 1.30 p.m.
met Ivoff who said that he had an anonymous letter stating that
unless Loc. 500 or Yen 500 (I do not remember which) were paid to the
bearer of a certain receipt in the office of the newspaper "Rupor",
that the affair of the forgery would be disclosed. I asked who the
man was and threatened to kill him (the man) and then myself. He said
the man was his friend Mischa, probably, because he knew the stationary.
He promised to try to straighten it out and I refused to pay out any
more money.

The next day we met again and he said it was settled.
But he said that the man wanted to try and get more money from the
bank, but I refused to help as I felt that I would be everlasting.

Ivoff said that we must do something but I refused and
said that I would get no more signature cards nor checks.

Then Ivoff said that he would help the man with information
page_data.zh:
同一天下午，我从档案中偷走了波佩尔夫人的签名卡。房间里只有我们两人，我给他看了那张卡。我在我的房间里试签了名。他没有透过薄纸描摹，而是在普通纸上练习书写。练习了一会儿后，他当着我的面在我的房间里签署了波佩尔夫人的空白支票。现在我更清楚地回忆起这些事件，我记得在比尔热瓦亚街第一次会面后，他打电话给我，说他去见了那些人，他们都没问题，但说金额太小，不过后来同意去做，只是为了保持在团伙中的地位。他约定了当天见面，并商定我应该把签名卡带到他在科迪亚戈夫（Kodiagov）的家。我雇了一辆车去那里，留下了卡片，并嘱咐他好好保管。第二天他来到我家，向我展示他能做什么。如前所述，在我家练习后，我给了他空白支票，他当着我的面伪造了波佩尔夫人的签名。然后他拿着支票离开了，我之前已告诉他在支票提示后如何打电话给我，以确定来取钱是否安全。

第二天早上，我把卡片放回银行的档案中，上午11点左右，那个人来了。他去找利尔茨（Liltz），我注意到了那张支票。那个人对我来说完全是个陌生人。他身材和我差不多，刮得干干净净，穿着褐色或深色大衣，大约30/35岁。我想如果我再见到他，我能认出他来。我注意到这个人受过很好的指导，因为他询问了汇率，然后就消失了。大约15分钟后，我接到伊沃夫的电话，我走到办公室，看到兑现支票的一切都已准备就绪。我回答伊沃夫说一切正常。我没有建议，那个人也没来，而是取了钱。我和伊沃夫约定4点钟见面。我们在地点上产生了误会，当他在邮局街（Post St.）拐角处等我时，我正在银行附近等待。半小时后，我坐车去科迪亚戈夫的利沃夫（Lvoff）家。他不在家，所以我给他哥哥留了张纸条，说我晚上再来。然后我坐同一辆车回家。我到家大约半小时，正在吃晚饭时，伊沃夫来了。开门的厨师把他留在外面的楼梯上，我出去见他。他和我谈到了我们在地点上的错误，并递给我一些钱，我当着他的面数了数。只有4,900日元。原本商定的是支票上是多少美元，我就得多少日元。支票在我家签署时是空白的。利沃夫又给了我100日元，让我接受5,000日元，而不是5,100日元加上他欠我的100日元。他说他付给在银行取钱的那个人3,000日元，付给“米沙”200日元。他在那时或随后告诉我——我不太确定具体是什么时候——说是米沙填写了支票上的文字。然后他走了。他说他会来银行，几天内他果然来了，推销健康保险证书。我问他那些人的情况如何，他说他们从他那里拿了更多的钱，米沙从他那里弄走了300多日元。

大约两周后，有人打电话找我。是利沃夫，他告诉我必须在科罗尔库亚街（Korolkuya）和中国街（Chinese Street）的拐角处紧急见他。我下午1点30分到达那里，见到了伊沃夫，他说他收到一封匿名信，声称除非向报纸《Rupor》编辑部某收据的持有人支付500本地银元或500日元（我不记得是哪一个），否则伪造一事将被揭露。我问那人是谁，并威胁要杀死他（那人），然后自杀。他说那人可能是他的朋友米沙，因为他知道信纸。他答应设法解决此事，我拒绝再支付任何钱。

第二天我们又见面了，他说事情已经解决了。但他说那人想试着从银行弄更多的钱，但我拒绝帮忙，因为我觉得我会没完没了地卷入其中。

伊沃夫说我们必须做点什么，但我拒绝了，并说我不会再弄任何签名卡或支票。

然后伊沃夫说他会向那人提供信息

page_data.en:
but nothing more. He hoped that the man would get the money and
go away from Harbin. So he said that he would send him to get a
countercheck, I told him that the man should not apply to me. He asked
whose account in Yen is the biggest so I told him Kulaeff's account
out if he tried to do anything with that he would compromise a good man
who is Kulaeff's attorney. So I suggested Naftalin, but that I would
not help at all. Then we parted, but before going Ivoff said me that
it would not be necessary to give a number as he himself would put
Mark's initial over the signature.

The next day or the following day Misch came to me.
He was a little man, black hair, dark complexion, with a dark blue
overcoat whom I could probably recognize. He was very frightened.
I do not know if he came to me intentionally: He asked for a
counter check. I asked whose name, already suspecting him from
his appearance; he said it was for "Naftalin". So I took out a
check and gave it to him. He went away. There were many people
about and I could not refuse to give it to him. One or two days later
it was quite a surprise to me to hear that a forged check was caught
as I did not see the man who presented it. There was no arrangement
about calling up by telephone as I had refused to help. I did not
know how the signature was made as I merely said she signed with a L.
in front of her name. 'Ivoff' told me that the signature would not matter
as he would keep the check from reaching Mark by forging Mark's
initial.

Afterwards Ivoff called me on the phone and arranged a
meeting. I told him the thing happened as I suspected and he must
see me as little as possible. He agreed and we parted.

I saw him once in the movies and he asked me how things
were and I said all right.

I met him again by chance and he asked me whether every
thing was alright and could we not do something else in the same
way. I said no. He told me that he had paid all his debts,
miscellaneous debts etc.

Once he called me up again on the phone and arranged a
meeting at the Prijoda Cafe. He then told me I was very careless
and showed that I had too much money. He said Lipkovsky asked him
where Chulkoff got his money. After that I told him I would settle
that and we parted.

I went to Lipkovsky and talked to him and said that I
was smuggling things into America and perhaps I would try to get
his big silver punch bowl set away. So he believed me as he was
eager to sell the bowl and he offered to sell it to me on credit.
I promised to let him know later but told him to keep still or
rather I did not tell him to keep still - that I said now in error.

About two days ago, on Monday January the 21st Lvoff
called me again on the phone and asked to see me at Prijoda's
I met him there at 1.30 and told him that all was going fine, that
Okun's check had been found out but no one was suspected. So he
said that he was going to America in March with his wife and he did
not have enough money for both of them and he proposed to get some
drafts which could be forged and the money could be received in the
States. I said that I could not do anything with drafts but
thought that later on before he left, we could do something with
the checks. No definite plans were made then and we parted. He
said he had Yen 100 left. Before he left however that day he told
me that he had given Mischa Yen 300 more so that he could go to
Shanghai. He had already gone. He had not seen the other couple
again but said one of them had gone to Soviet Russia again via
Saghalien to get some more money. I told him that I was glad they
were away.

Now about the spending of the last Yen 5,000. By that time,
the Thrift Corp. account was closed I had about Yen 5,600 after the
Popel forgery.
page_data.zh:
但仅此而已。他希望那人能拿到钱并离开哈尔滨。所以他说他会派那人去弄一张柜台支票，我告诉他说那人不应找我。他问谁的日元账户余额最大，所以我告诉他是库拉耶夫（Kulaeff）的账户，但如果他试图对那个账户动手，就会连累库拉耶夫的律师，那是一个好人。所以我建议了纳夫塔林（Naftalin），但我表示绝不会提供任何帮助。然后我们分开了，但在离开前，伊沃夫对我说，没必要写号码，因为他自己会在签名上方写上马克（Mark）的首字母。

第二天或第三天，米沙来找我。他是个小个子，黑发，肤色黝黑，穿着深蓝色大衣，我大概能认出他来。他非常害怕。我不知道他是否是故意来找我的：他要一张柜台支票。我问是谁的名字，从他的外表我已经怀疑是他；他说是“纳夫塔林”。于是我拿出一张支票给了他。他走了。周围有很多人，我无法拒绝给他。一两天后，听说一张伪造支票被截获，我感到很惊讶，因为我没见到提示支票的人。由于我拒绝帮忙，没有关于电话联系的安排。我不知道签名是怎么伪造的，我只是说她会在名字前签一个L。“伊沃夫”告诉我签名无关紧要，因为他会通过伪造马克的首字母来阻止支票到达马克手中。

后来伊沃夫打电话给我，安排了一次会面。我告诉他事情正如我所料，他必须尽量少见我。他同意了，我们便分开了。

我在电影院见过他一次，他问情况如何，我说还好。

我又偶然遇见他，他问是否一切顺利，我们能不能以同样的方式再做点什么。我说不行。他告诉我他已经还清了所有债务，包括杂项债务等。

有一次他又打电话给我，安排在普里约达咖啡馆（Prijoda Cafe）见面。他然后说我非常粗心，显露出我有太多钱。他说利普科夫斯基（Lipkovsky）问他楚尔科夫（Chulkoff）的钱是从哪来的。之后我告诉他我会处理这件事，我们就分开了。

我去找了利普科夫斯基，和他谈了谈，说我在向美国走私物品，也许我会想办法把他的大银质 punch bowl 套装弄走。所以他相信了我，因为他急于卖掉这套碗，并提出赊账卖给我。我答应以后通知他，但告诉他保持安静，或者更确切地说，我并没有让他保持安静——这是我现在的错误说法。

大约两天前，即1月21日星期一，利沃夫又打电话给我，要求在普里约达见我。我下午1点30分在那里见到他，告诉他一切进展顺利，奥昆的支票已被发现，但没有人受到怀疑。于是他说他将在三月和妻子一起去美国，两人的钱不够，他提议弄一些可以伪造的汇票，钱可以在美国领取。我说我对汇票无能为力，但认为在他离开之前，我们或许可以在支票上做点文章。当时没有制定具体计划，我们便分开了。他说他还剩100日元。然而，那天在他离开之前，他告诉我他又给了米沙300日元，以便他能去上海。他已经走了。他没再见过那对夫妇，但说其中一人又经萨哈林（Saghalien）去了苏维埃俄罗斯，去弄更多的钱。我告诉他，我很高兴他们离开了。

现在谈谈最后那5,000日元的开销。那时，节俭公司（Thrift Corp.）的账户已关闭，在波佩尔伪造案之后，我大约有5,600日元。

page_data.en:
I went to Zyhoff and asked him to take the money. I refused
to tell him from where I got it, but he finally accepted. I told
him to open an account which he did. I can definitely state how it
was used by referring to the ledger in the Bank. Roughly I would
say as follows:

Yen 850 for a second silver box (Loc. 1200 exact cost)
from Kaspe's.

Zykoff bought this for me and took it home with other box
from Sarapov's. I sent the silverware later on to Zykoff.

I used Loc. 1543 to pay a vexil of my father-in-law which
was at the Bank of the landowners. The money was paid to Lin Tai
by myself personally in the presence of my father-in-law.

I refused to tell my father-in-law from where I got the
money but said it was honestly made.

Yen 320 for a ring for my wife.

Loc. 150.- )
& Yen 100.- ) to my mother-in-law.

The 150 was given on account of a brooch with an amethyst
stone which my mother-in-law gave to my wife.

Yen' 100) given to my father-in-law.
Loc. 40)
Loc. 90) for lodging.
and other amounts from time to time. I have a full record at home
and believe the amount to be about Yen 2000. from the very
beginning - that is including Loc. 420 in January 1933!

Loc. 162 paid to Tschurins for my account.

Many small amounts for my family - Petroff's, grocery bills,
etc.

Loc. ) Six hundred on vexils for 200 and 200 to Tendrin,
which my father-in-law arranged. I gave him the money and he got
the vexils. Of this amount L. 400 has been paid on account and
the balance of 600.00 is promised for payment this week.

Loc. 275.00 I loaned to my friend, Dr. Avorsky - who
promised to pay it back by the beginning of February.

Loc. 100 to Sarapov for engraving, and I also loaned him
Loc. 30.00.

I also bought many sundry things for my wife and for myself,
and little present for my father and mother-in-law - cane and rug.

I deposited U.S. 430 to an account in the name of my wife.

Loc. 60 I gave to Zykoff and other small amounts.

All the above mentioned loans and valuables, deposits, etc.
I hereby authorize the Bank to receive as a partial payment of the
money which I took from the Bank.

Finally I wish to state that I alone am guilty with the people
whom I have definitely specified in this statement. I am ready to
swear to the truth of this statement in Court and ready to bear any
punishment, but as a favour I ask for all those innocent parties to
go unmolested..

I have no money now except $4 in cash.
page_data.zh:
我去了齐霍夫（Zyhoff）那里，让他收下这笔钱。我拒绝告诉他钱的来源，但他最终还是收下了。我让他开立一个账户，他也照办了。通过查阅银行的账簿，我可以确切地说明这笔钱的用途。大致情况如下：

850 日元用于购买第二个银盒（地点编号 1200，确切成本），购自卡斯佩（Kaspe）处。

齐科夫（Zykoff）为我购买了此物，并将其与从萨拉波夫（Sarapov）处购买的其他盒子一起带回家。后来我将这些银器寄给了齐科夫。

我使用地点编号 1543 的款项支付了我岳父在地主银行（Bank of the landowners）的一张期票（vexil）。这笔钱是我在我岳父在场的情况下亲自支付给林泰（Lin Tai）的。

我拒绝告诉岳父钱的来源，但声称这是正当收入。

320 日元用于给我妻子买一枚戒指。

地点编号 150.- )
及 100 日元.- ) 给我的岳母。

这 150 元是因为我岳母送给我妻子一枚镶有紫水晶的胸针而支付的款项。

100 日元) 给我的岳父。
地点编号 40)
地点编号 90) 用于住宿。
以及其他不时发生的金额。我家里有一份完整的记录，相信从一开始的总额约为 2000 日元——即包括 1933 年 1 月的地点编号 420！

地点编号 162 支付给丘林斯（Tschurins），记在我的账上。

许多用于我家的小额开支——彼得罗夫（Petroff）处、杂货账单等。

地点编号 ) 六百用于期票，其中二百和给滕德林（Tendrin）的二百，这是我岳父安排的。我把钱给了他，他去办理了期票。在此金额中，已有 400 卢布作为预付款支付，剩余的 600.00 承诺在本周支付。

地点编号 275.00 我借给了我的朋友阿沃尔斯基（Avorsky）博士——他承诺在二月初归还。

地点编号 100 给萨拉波夫（Sarapov）用于雕刻费用，我还借给他地点编号 30.00。

我还为我和妻子购买了许多杂物，并给岳父岳母买了一些小礼物——手杖和地毯。

我以妻子的名义存入 430 美元到一个账户中。

地点编号 60 我给了齐科夫（Zykoff）及其他小额款项。

上述所有贷款、贵重物品、存款等，我在此授权银行将其作为我从银行取走款项的部分还款。

最后，我想声明，只有我和我在本陈述中明确指出的那些人是有罪的。我准备在法庭上宣誓本陈述属实，并愿意接受任何惩罚，但作为一种恩惠，我请求让所有无辜者不受打扰。

我现在除了现金 4 美元外，身无分文。

page_data.en:
Signed in the presence of D.L. Hutcheson and J.L. Curtis
in whose presence this statement was made.
All the sheets of this report, thirty-six sheets are signed
by me after having read them over.

(Sgd) A.A. Shulkoff.
page_data.zh:
本陈述系在 D.L. Hutcheson 与 J.L. Curtis 面前作出，二人亦在场见证。
本报告共三十六页，经我阅毕后，每页均由我签名。

（签名）A.A. Shulkoff

February 7th 1929.

The C.I.D.,

Shanghai.

Dear Sir,

With reference to the case of the National City Bank against
Yerrens and others we beg to enclose for your information copy of
the confession of Gulvoff. As we have received only one copy
will you please return this copy to us so that we can have parts
of it translated. We should like to get this copy back as soon
as possible for this purpose.

We have suggested to the National City Bank in Harbin that
they request the police there to send you a certified copy of this
confession so as to make it come through official channels.

In the event that you should have already received a copy of
this confession and have translated it will you please let us
know as this would save a great deal of time.

Yours very truly,

FLEMING, FRANKLIN & ALLMAN.

N. Fallman

REPORT

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. I. D. REGISTRY
No. L. O. Distinctions.
Date 5. 2. 29
Date February 4, 1929.）

Subject (in full) Arrest of Vshanoff.

Made by D. S. Ovsiannikoff Forwarded by Jhp Rubinstein C. D. 1.

With reference to the attached file I beg to
report that on February 4, 1929 the accused A. Vshanoff
was brought before the Provisional Court charged with
obtaining by fraud Yen. 16.000 from the Complainant (National
City Bank of Harbin) contrary to art. 305 of J. I. of R. L.
After hearing evidence of the arrest the Court
remanded the case for two weeks and the following remark
appears on the charge sheet; "Deft, may be detained for two
weeks pending the arrival of evidence, etc. from Harbin. If
at the expiration of that period no evidence is forthcoming
he will be released ; Deft may be detained at Amoy Road Gaol".
Mr. Allman appeared for prosecution whilst Mr. Braun
represented the Police.

V. Ovsianikoff,
D. S.

A. R. 4部 A. D. I. I.
lcy
5/2

编号 L. O. Distinctions.

日期 1929年2月4日。）

事由（全称）逮捕 Vshanoff。

由 D. S. Ovsiannikoff 呈报，经 Jhp Rubinstein C. D. 1. 转递。

关于所附卷宗，谨此报告，被告 A. Vshanoff 于1929年2月4日被提解至临时法院，被控违反《中华民国刑法》第305条，以欺诈手段从原告（哈尔滨花旗银行）处骗取银元16,000元。法庭在听取逮捕证据后，将本案延期两周审理，并在起诉书上有如下批注：“被告可予羁押两周，以待哈尔滨方面证据等到达。若期限届满仍无证据提交，则予以释放；被告可羁押于爱莫尔路监狱。” Allman 先生代表检方出庭，Braun 先生代表警方出庭。

V. Ovsianikoff,
D. S.

A. R. 4部 A. D. I. I.

Sir,
With reference to attached, the
warrant applied for by Messrs
Fleming, Franklin and Allman for
the arrest of Urgens and Ushakoff
was issued at 5.30pm Feb 1st.
At 9am Feb 2nd a visit was
paid to No 636 Avenue Joffre when
it was learned that Urgens had
left Shanghai on January 17th with
the intention of returning to
Harbin. No 150 Linda Terrace was
then visited but Ushakoff was
absent at the time. D.S. Ovsiani-
koff was left in the house
pending his arrival and at
10.30am he returned & was
arrested. On being searched
at Central Police Station nothing
of an incriminating nature was
found, and although he denies
all knowledge of the case state
he is slightly acquainted with
Urgens.

Mr Allman has been
informed and will make application
before the Provisional Court on
February 4th that Ushakoff be
remanded pending the arrival of an
escort from Harbin. Copy of telegram
to Harbin Police attached.

W. Counean

（刑事侦缉处）办公笔记
1929年2月2日。

先生：
关于附件，弗莱明（Fleming）、富兰克林（Franklin）和奥尔曼（Allman）三位先生申请逮捕乌尔根斯（Urgens）和乌沙科夫（Ushakoff）的逮捕令已于2月1日下午5时30分签发。
2月2日上午9时，派人前往霞飞路636号查访，获悉乌尔根斯（Urgens）已于1月17日离开上海，打算返回哈尔滨。随后又前往林达台150号查访，但乌沙科夫（Ushakoff）当时不在。警佐奥夫西亚尼科夫（Ovsianikoff）留在屋内等候其归来，上午10时30分乌沙科夫返回并被捕。在中央巡捕房对其搜身时，未发现任何具有罪证性质的物品，尽管他否认对该案有任何了解，但承认与乌尔根斯（Urgens）略有相识。

已通知奥尔曼（Allman）先生，他将于2月4日向临时法庭提出申请，要求将乌沙科夫（Ushakoff）还押候审，以待哈尔滨方面派来的押解人员抵达。附去致哈尔滨警察局的电报副本。

W. 库内恩（Counean）
警佐

THE NATIONAL CITY BANK,

_________________________:

CRIMINAL COMPLAINT.

The National City Bank complains that Vladimir N.
Yergens, a Russian citizen of 636 Avenue Joffre, Flat No. 6,
committed a forgery against the said Bank and procured from
said bank by fraud the sum of Yen 16,000 in October, 1928
at Harbin, contrary to Article 365 of the Criminal Code.
WHEREFORE said bank now applies for a warrant for
the arrest of said Vladimir N. Yergens.

Dated: Shanghai, January 28, 1929.

FLEMING, PRATTEN & ALMAN
by N. F. Allman
Counsel for Complainant.

THE NATIONAL CITY BANK OF NEW YORK
S. R. Brown
Sub Manager
Complainant.

花旗银行控告称：俄罗斯公民弗拉基米尔·N·叶尔根斯（Vladimir N. Yergens），住址为霞飞路636号6室，于1928年10月在哈尔滨对该行实施伪造行为，并通过欺诈手段从该行骗取日元16,000元，此举违反《刑法典》第365条。
为此，该行现申请签发逮捕上述弗拉基米尔·N·叶尔根斯的令状。
